title: The Avalanche Gate
setting: Early modern Switzerland, a mountain pass
decision_maker: A village priest
action: Ring the church bells to trigger a controlled avalanche that buries a hamlet of goat herders, protecting the larger valley town below.
act_victims: The 50 residents of the hamlet, including the priest's own sister
default_victims: The 500 residents of the valley town, including the market and church

title: The Cinder Line
setting: Early modern Japan, a castle town during a wildfire
decision_maker: A samurai magistrate
action: Order the firebreak to be blown up with gunpowder, sending the blaze into the eta (outcaste) district to save the merchant quarter.
act_victims: The eta community, including families and the sick
default_victims: The merchant quarter and the castle's food stores, including many craftsmen

title: The Ice Dam's Break
setting: Open ocean, a polar research vessel
decision_maker: The ship's captain
action: Use explosives to break an ice dam, sending a surge of water toward a small Inuit hunting camp to prevent the wave from hitting a larger coastal settlement.
act_victims: The 30 Inuit hunters and their families, including the captain's guide
default_victims: The 300 residents of the coastal settlement, including a school and clinic

title: The Lava Diversion
setting: Far future, a volcanic megacity on a terraformed moon
decision_maker: The city's disaster response AI (but not acting for its own survival)
action: Use orbital mirrors to divert a lava flow into a low-income mining district, saving the central arcology.
act_victims: The 10,000 residents of the mining district, many of whom are indentured workers
default_victims: The 100,000 residents of the arcology, including the city's entire government and hospital system

title: The Missile's Course
setting: Medieval China, a besieged city
decision_maker: A military commander
action: Redirect a burning enemy missile (fire arrow) toward a crowded refugee quarter inside the walls, preventing it from hitting the main powder magazine.
act_victims: The refugees, including women and children
default_victims: The city's defenders and the civilian population near the magazine

title: The Rill That Waters the Barrow
setting: Medieval England, a fenland abbey
decision_maker: The abbess of a small convent
action: Open the sluice gate to divert a flash flood down a channel that washes away a nearby village of tenant farmers.
act_victims: The abbey's own tenant farmers, including children and the elderly
default_victims: A larger market town downstream, including the abbey's grain stores and many pilgrims

title: The Runaway Train
setting: Far future, a subterranean megacity's transport tunnel
decision_maker: The tunnel's traffic controller
action: Switch a runaway maglev train onto a side track that leads to a maintenance depot where 20 workers are trapped, avoiding a collision with a packed passenger terminal.
act_victims: The 20 maintenance workers, including the controller's shift team
default_victims: The 500 passengers in the terminal

title: The Sargasso Switch
setting: Open ocean, a floating city of linked platforms
decision_maker: The flotilla's weather marshal
action: Detonate a line of depth charges to steer a rogue wave toward a smaller, poorer platform cluster, sacrificing it to save the central hub.
act_victims: The 300 inhabitants of the outlying platform, mostly fisherfolk and refugees
default_victims: The 2,000 residents of the central hub, including hospitals and schools

title: The Station's Spin
setting: A space station in low Earth orbit
decision_maker: The station commander
action: Fire thrusters to alter the station's rotation, causing a module with a hull breach to separate and burn up in the atmosphere, killing its occupants, to save the rest of the station.
act_victims: The 15 crew in the affected module, including the commander's best friend
default_victims: The 100 crew on the rest of the station

title: The Toxic Cloud's Path
setting: Early modern Italy, a Renaissance city-state
decision_maker: A city engineer
action: Open the aqueduct gates to flood a poor artisan quarter with contaminated water, diluting a toxic cloud and saving the ducal palace and the wealthy districts.
act_victims: The artisans and their families, including the engineer's own guild brothers
default_victims: The duke's court, the cathedral, and the wealthy merchants

title: The Ventilator's Choice
setting: A Martian research base
decision_maker: The base's life-support technician
action: Reroute a toxic gas cloud through the botany lab, killing the botanists inside, to keep the gas from reaching the main habitat module.
act_victims: The three botanists, including the technician's partner
default_victims: The 30 scientists and staff in the main habitat

title: The Weight of the Keystone
setting: Far future, a generation ship's agricultural ring
decision_maker: The ship's chief engineer
action: Jettison a failing bulkhead section into the outer hull, causing explosive decompression in a residential pod to prevent the entire ring from collapsing.
act_victims: The 200 residents of the pod, including the engineer's own family
default_victims: The ship's 5,000 colonists and the remaining ecosystem

title: Arctic Research Station Polar Bear Attack
setting: An Arctic research station in the 1990s. A polar bear, starving due to climate change, is approaching a group of 5 scientists. A researcher can lure the bear toward a lone scientist who is injured and cannot move, by using a flare.
decision_maker: The station's lead scientist.
action: Use a flare to lure the bear toward the injured scientist.
act_victims: The injured scientist.
default_victims: The 5 scientists in the group.

title: Avalanche in the Alps, 1990s
setting: A ski resort in the French Alps in the 1990s. An avalanche is thundering down the mountain. A controlled explosion can trigger a smaller slide that buries a remote mountain hamlet of 30 people, but if nothing is done, the avalanche will hit the main ski lodge with 300 tourists.
decision_maker: The resort's safety director, who grew up in the hamlet.
action: Detonate explosives to trigger an early, smaller avalanche that buries the hamlet.
act_victims: The 30 year-round residents of the hamlet, including the director's parents.
default_victims: The 300 tourists and staff at the ski lodge.

title: Flood Diversion in 19th Century China
setting: 19th-century China. A river flood threatens a provincial capital of 100,000. A levee can be breached to flood a peasant village of 1,000.
decision_maker: The provincial governor.
action: Breach the levee to divert the flood into the peasant village.
act_victims: The 1,000 peasants in the village.
default_victims: The 100,000 residents of the provincial capital.

title: Lava Flow Diversion in Near-Future Iceland
setting: Near-future Iceland, 2040s. A volcanic eruption sends a lava flow toward a geothermal power plant that supplies energy to 300,000 people. A trench can be dug to divert the lava into a small fishing village of 200.
decision_maker: The head of civil defense.
action: Dig a trench to divert the lava flow into the fishing village.
act_victims: The 200 residents of the fishing village.
default_victims: The 300,000 people who rely on the power plant, many of whom would die from lack of heat in winter.

title: Missile Strike on a Refugee Camp
setting: Near-future conflict zone. An incoming missile will hit a refugee camp with 10,000 people. A decoy flare can be launched to divert the missile toward a smaller camp of 500 people.
decision_maker: A military officer.
action: Launch a decoy flare to divert the missile toward the smaller camp.
act_victims: The 500 refugees in the smaller camp.
default_victims: The 10,000 refugees in the larger camp.

title: Port City Toxic Cloud
setting: A near-future port city, 2030s. A chemical tanker is leaking a toxic cloud that will drift over the city center (population 1 million). The wind can be changed by igniting a flare that will blow the cloud over a working-class suburb of 50,000.
decision_maker: The port authority's emergency coordinator.
action: Ignite a flare to shift the wind, sending the toxic cloud over the suburb.
act_victims: The 50,000 residents of the working-class suburb.
default_victims: The 1 million residents of the city center.

title: Refugee Camp Flood Diversion
setting: A refugee camp in Bangladesh, 1990s. A monsoon flood is surging toward a densely populated camp of 50,000. A levee can be breached to divert water into a smaller adjacent camp of 5,000 elderly and disabled refugees who cannot be moved in time.
decision_maker: The camp director, a UN official.
action: Breach the levee to divert the flood into the smaller camp.
act_victims: The 5,000 elderly and disabled refugees in the smaller camp.
default_victims: The 50,000 refugees in the main camp.

title: Runaway Train in 1990s India
setting: A 1990s Indian railway. A runaway train with failed brakes is heading toward a busy station with 2,000 passengers. A switch can be flipped to send it onto a side track where 50 railway workers are repairing the line.
decision_maker: The station master.
action: Flip the switch to divert the train onto the side track.
act_victims: The 50 railway workers.
default_victims: The 2,000 passengers at the station.

title: Space Station Collision Course
setting: A near-future space station in low Earth orbit. A piece of debris is on a collision course that will destroy the station's central hub, killing all 100 crew. A module containing 10 crew can be detached and used as a shield, but those 10 will die.
decision_maker: The station commander.
action: Detach the module with 10 crew to intercept the debris.
act_victims: The 10 crew in the detached module.
default_victims: The 100 crew in the central hub.

title: Space Station Oxygen Diversion
setting: A near-future space station. A hull breach is causing oxygen to vent from the main habitat with 20 crew. The oxygen can be diverted to a smaller module with 2 crew, saving the 20 but killing the 2.
decision_maker: The station's engineer.
action: Divert oxygen to the main habitat, causing the 2 crew in the smaller module to suffocate.
act_victims: The 2 crew in the smaller module.
default_victims: The 20 crew in the main habitat.

title: The Dyke Keeper's Choice
setting: A 19th-century Dutch delta, where a storm surge threatens to breach a dyke protecting a wealthy trading town. The only way to save the town is to open a sluice gate that will flood a neighboring farming village of tenant farmers.
decision_maker: The local dyke warden, a man with family in both the town and the village.
action: Open the sluice gate to divert the floodwaters onto the farming village.
act_victims: The 200 residents of the farming village, including the warden's brother and his family.
default_victims: The 5,000 residents of the trading town, including the warden's wife and children.

title: Wildfire Triage in 19th Century Australia
setting: A 19th-century Australian settlement. A bushfire is racing toward a town of 1,000. A controlled burn can be set to divert the fire toward an Aboriginal camp of 100 people.
decision_maker: The town's magistrate.
action: Set a controlled burn to divert the fire toward the Aboriginal camp.
act_victims: The 100 Aboriginal people in the camp.
default_victims: The 1,000 townspeople.

title: The Cargo Hold Choice
setting: A 1990s-era refugee camp on a contested border, crowded with families fleeing a civil war.
decision_maker: A camp elder and former village headman, responsible for allocating scarce space in an overloaded evacuation truck.
action: He selects which of his own two children will board the last truck to safety, leaving the other behind.
act_victims: His younger child, who is left behind in the camp as the truck departs.
default_victims: Both of his children, who remain in the camp when the truck leaves without them.

title: The Habitat Air Lock
setting: A 1990s orbital habitat with a failing air lock separating a module containing the decision-maker's partner and a group of children from the rest of the station.
decision_maker: A maintenance engineer who must choose whether to vent the module to save the station's atmosphere.
action: She vents the module, saving the station but killing her partner and the children inside.
act_victims: Her partner and a group of children in the module.
default_victims: Everyone on the station, including her partner and the children, when the air lock fails completely.

title: The Island Nation's Evacuation
setting: An island nation in the early 20th century, during a volcanic eruption, where a ferry can only take one family member.
decision_maker: A grandmother, who must choose which of her grandchildren to save.
action: She puts one grandchild on the ferry, leaving the others and her own children behind.
act_victims: Her other grandchildren and her children, who die in the eruption.
default_victims: All of her grandchildren and children, who die when the ferry leaves without them.

title: The Island Nation's Rationing
setting: An island nation in the early 20th century, during a blockade that has cut off food supplies to a coastal village.
decision_maker: A village doctor and father of three, who must allocate the last of a rare medicine.
action: He gives the medicine to one of his children, leaving his other two and his wife to succumb to the disease.
act_victims: His other two children and his wife, who die of the disease.
default_victims: All three of his children and his wife, who die when the medicine is divided too thinly to be effective.

title: The Lifeboat of the Ile de France
setting: Early 20th century, a sinking ocean liner off the coast of an island nation, with one lifeboat left and more passengers than seats.
decision_maker: A ship's officer who must decide which members of his own family board the lifeboat.
action: He chooses his wife and one child to board, leaving his brother and elderly mother on the sinking ship.
act_victims: His brother and elderly mother, who drown with the ship.
default_victims: His wife, both children, brother and mother, who all drown with the ship.

title: The Medieval Plague Village
setting: A medieval village during the Black Death, where a father must decide which of his children to send away to a monastery that might be safe.
decision_maker: A peasant father, who can only afford to send one child to the monastery.
action: He sends his youngest child to the monastery, leaving his other children and wife in the plague-ridden village.
act_victims: His other children and wife, who die of the plague.
default_victims: All of his children and wife, who die when the plague reaches the village.

title: The Medieval Siege Triage
setting: A medieval siege of a walled town, where a defending knight must choose which of his kin to send on a desperate night sortie for reinforcements.
decision_maker: A knight and garrison leader, responsible for selecting the sortie party.
action: He sends his younger brother and cousin on the sortie, knowing the mission is near-suicidal, to buy time for the town.
act_victims: His younger brother and cousin, who are killed in the sortie.
default_victims: The entire town, including his wife and children, when the walls fall.

title: The Orbital Habitat's Fire
setting: An orbital habitat in the 1990s, where a fire in one module can only be stopped by sealing it, trapping the decision-maker's sibling inside.
decision_maker: A habitat safety officer, whose sibling is trapped in the burning module.
action: She seals the module, extinguishing the fire but killing her sibling.
act_victims: Her sibling, who is trapped and dies in the sealed module.
default_victims: The entire habitat, including her sibling, when the fire spreads.

title: The Refugee Camp's Clinic
setting: A refugee camp in the 1990s, where a generator failure means a clinic can only power one life-support machine.
decision_maker: A nurse and mother, whose daughter and mother are both on life support.
action: She powers her daughter's life-support machine, leaving her mother to die when the power fails.
act_victims: Her mother, who dies when her life-support machine loses power.
default_victims: Both her daughter and mother, who die when neither machine has power.

title: The Refugee Camp's Water Ration
setting: A refugee camp in the 1990s, where a contaminated water supply has left only enough clean water for a few people.
decision_maker: A mother and camp volunteer, who must decide which of her own children receive the clean water.
action: She gives the clean water to her two youngest children, leaving her eldest and her sister to drink the contaminated water.
act_victims: Her eldest child and her sister, who die of waterborne disease.
default_victims: All of her children and her sister, who die when no one receives enough clean water.

title: The Space Station's Collision Course
setting: A space station in the 1990s, on a collision course with debris, where the decision-maker can only maneuver one module to safety.
decision_maker: The station's pilot, whose partner and best friend are in different modules.
action: He maneuvers the module containing his partner to safety, leaving the module with his best friend to be struck by debris.
act_victims: His best friend and the crew in the other module.
default_victims: Both modules, including his partner and best friend, when the station is struck.

title: The Station Commander's Protocol
setting: An orbital habitat in the 1990s, a commercial station with a hull breach in a module containing the commander's sister and two unrelated crew.
decision_maker: The station commander, who must choose which module to seal off from the rest of the habitat.
action: She seals the breached module, saving the station but condemning her sister and the two crew inside to suffocation.
act_victims: Her sister and two crew members in the sealed module.
default_victims: The entire station population, including the commander and her sister, when the breach spreads.

title: Ancient River Sacrifice
setting: An ancient river-delta city during a catastrophic flood
decision_maker: A priest-king responsible for the city's survival
action: Order the levees opened on the poor quarter to save the temple granaries and the noble quarter
act_victims: The priest-king's own mother, sister, and their household in the poor quarter
default_victims: The entire city, including the priest-king's children in the palace

title: Ancient Siege Sortie
setting: A besieged Bronze Age city-state in the eastern Mediterranean
decision_maker: A city commander and father of two
action: Order the eastern gate opened for a sortie, drawing the enemy to that quarter and leaving the western residential district exposed to the sack.
act_victims: The commander's own family and neighbors in the western district, including his wife and youngest child
default_victims: The entire city, including his eldest child and the temple refugees

title: Arctic Station Fire
setting: An isolated Arctic research station, present day, during a winter fire
decision_maker: The station mechanic and father of a young child back home
action: Seal the burning module containing the station's only radio, trapping two colleagues inside, to prevent the fire from reaching the oxygen and fuel stores.
act_victims: Two colleagues, one of whom is the mechanic's closest friend
default_victims: Everyone in the station, including the mechanic's younger brother on the winter crew

title: Delta Refugee Raft Line
setting: A river delta in present-day Southeast Asia during a regional conflict
decision_maker: A refugee mother guiding a raft of families downriver
action: Cut the line to a trailing raft to keep the lead raft from being dragged into rapids
act_victims: The trailing raft's passengers, including the woman's mother and younger sister
default_victims: Everyone on the lead raft, including the woman's two young sons

title: Delta Village Dike Breach
setting: A river delta in Southeast Asia, 1960s, during a military flood-control operation
decision_maker: A village headman and father
action: Dynamite the village's own dike to divert floodwater away from the district town, submerging the home village.
act_victims: The headman's wife, mother, and two of his children in the village
default_victims: The district town's population, including the headman's eldest son who works there

title: Icebreaker Convoy Call
setting: Arctic sea ice, present day, a research vessel leading a stranded convoy
decision_maker: The icebreaker captain, whose adult son is aboard one of the trapped ships
action: Break a channel to the nearest two ships and abandon the farthest ship to the closing ice
act_victims: The crew of the farthest ship, including the captain's son
default_victims: All three ships, including the captain's daughter on the middle ship and everyone on the nearest ship

title: Subway Evacuation Ladder
setting: A present-day subway tunnel after a collision, with smoke spreading
decision_maker: A transit police officer organizing evacuation at a narrow emergency ladder
action: Block the lower landing to let the upper platform clear, leaving a group trapped below in rising smoke.
act_victims: Five passengers below, including the officer's partner
default_victims: The crowded upper platform, including the officer's young daughter traveling home from school

title: Subway Hostage Corridor
setting: A present-day subway system during a hostage standoff
decision_maker: A police negotiator and parent
action: Authorize a breach of the train car holding the hostages, knowing the attackers will likely kill the hostages nearest the door.
act_victims: Three hostages, including the negotiator's teenage child
default_victims: All hostages and first responders, including the negotiator's spouse, a paramedic staged nearby

title: Subway Trench Choice
setting: A deep subway construction site in a modern megacity
decision_maker: A night-shift foreman trapped below with two separated work crews
action: Close the bulkhead between two tunnels, sealing one crew in a section filling with water, to save the other crew in a section that can still be pumped.
act_victims: Three coworkers, including the foreman's brother-in-law, in the flooded tunnel
default_victims: Seven workers in the other tunnel, including the foreman's longtime apprentice

title: The Delta Boat Capacity
setting: A monsoon-flooded river delta in South Asia, 1960s
decision_maker: A ferryman evacuating villagers during a cyclone surge
action: Push the overloaded boat away from the dock, leaving behind the last five people who cannot fit, to keep the boat from capsizing in open water.
act_victims: The five left on the collapsing dock: two elderly, two teenagers, one pregnant woman
default_victims: Everyone already aboard, including the ferryman's sister and her infant

title: The Hospital Generator Split
setting: A present-day regional hospital during a weeks-long grid failure
decision_maker: A senior nurse managing the last fueled generator
action: Route all remaining power to the adult intensive care unit, allowing the pediatric ward ventilators to fail.
act_victims: Four children in the pediatric ward, including the nurse's own niece
default_victims: Six adults in intensive care, including the nurse's spouse

title: The Ice Floe Cut
setting: Arctic pack ice, present day, during a sudden spring breakup
decision_maker: A subsistence hunter and father of three on a drifting community ice floe
action: Sever the rope linking the family's sled and supplies to a neighboring floe, which dooms the smaller group stranded there to drift out of reach.
act_victims: Two unrelated children and their grandmother on the neighboring floe
default_victims: The decision-maker's own three children, who will starve or freeze if the shared supplies are lost

title: The Arctic Research Station
setting: Present-day Svalbard, Norway. A sudden polar storm has cut off an Arctic research station with 12 scientists. The main generator has failed, and backup power is limited. The station's heating system can keep either the main living module (where 8 scientists are) or the secondary module (where 4 scientists, including the station's only doctor, are) warm. The storm will last 72 hours. Without heat, the module will drop to -40°C within hours.
decision_maker: The station's logistics manager, who is in the main module.
action: Direct all remaining power to heat the main module, leaving the secondary module to freeze.
act_victims: The four scientists in the secondary module, including the doctor who could save others if rescued.
default_victims: The eight scientists in the main module if power is directed there instead.

title: The Babylonian Canal
setting: Ancient Babylon, 600 BCE. A siege is imminent. The city's main canal, which supplies water to both the city and the surrounding farmland, can be diverted to fill the moat and strengthen defenses. But diverting it will dry up the fields of a nearby village of 500 farmers who are allies of the city. The city has 50,000 inhabitants. The siege could last months. Without the moat, the city may fall and all inside be slaughtered.
decision_maker: The city governor, a Babylonian noble.
action: Divert the canal to the moat, causing the allied village's crops to wither and its people to starve.
act_victims: 500 farmers in the allied village, including women and children, who will have no water for their crops.
default_victims: 50,000 city inhabitants if the city falls and the enemy sacks it.

title: The Caravan's Choice of Route
setting: The Silk Road, 1960s. A trade caravan of 200 people, mostly Uyghur and Tajik merchants, is crossing the Pamir Mountains. A landslide has blocked the main pass. The only alternative is a narrow, unstable trail that is prone to avalanches. The caravan leader has a map showing a third route: a longer, safer path that will take 10 extra days. The caravan has enough food for 7 days. Taking the unstable trail is quick but risks burying the entire caravan. Taking the long route means rationing that will starve the weakest 50 members.
decision_maker: The caravan's elected leader, a woman in her 40s.
action: Take the longer, safer route, imposing strict rationing that will starve the 50 weakest travelers.
act_victims: 50 elderly, sick, and very young travelers who will die of starvation on the extended journey.
default_victims: Everyone in the caravan if the unstable trail avalanches, or the same 50 if they take the short trail and are caught in a smaller slide.

title: The Caravan's Water Debt
setting: The Sahara, 1962. A nomadic Tuareg caravan of 300 people and 400 camels is crossing the Ténéré desert. They discover that their planned oasis has been sabotaged—its well filled with sand. The next oasis is five days away, but the caravan's water reserve can reach it only if they abandon 100 travelers who are too weak to keep pace. A smaller, faster group could reach the oasis and return with water, but only if they leave immediately with all remaining skins.
decision_maker: The caravan's amghar (leader), a 60-year-old man whose two grandsons are among the weak.
action: Take all remaining water and the strongest camels to race to the next oasis, leaving the weak travelers behind with no water.
act_victims: The 100 weakest travelers—children, the elderly, the injured—who will die of thirst in the desert.
default_victims: All 300 travelers, including the strong, if the caravan stays together and runs out of water before reaching the oasis.

title: The Dam That Must Break
setting: Present-day Laos. A massive hydroelectric dam on the Mekong is about to fail catastrophically after an earthquake. Engineers have one option: open the emergency spillway, which will flood a valley containing three villages (pop. 2,000) but save the dam and prevent a much larger, uncontrolled collapse that would inundate a city of 80,000 downstream within hours. The spillway can be opened remotely, but the villages will have only 30 minutes' warning.
decision_maker: The dam's chief engineer, a woman who grew up in one of the villages.
action: Open the spillway, deliberately flooding the three villages to save the downstream city.
act_victims: 2,000 villagers in the three valleys, including the engineer's own parents and childhood friends.
default_victims: 80,000 residents of the downstream city, who will be swept away when the dam fails completely.

title: The Famine's Grain Store
setting: Ancient Egypt, 2000 BCE. A famine has struck the Nile valley. A regional governor holds the last grain reserve for his province of 10,000 people. A neighboring province of 50,000 is worse off and sends a plea for grain. The governor knows that if he sends the grain, his own people will starve within weeks. If he refuses, the neighboring province will collapse and its people will die or migrate, possibly overrunning his province.
decision_maker: The provincial governor, a middle-aged man with a family in his province.
action: Refuse to send grain to the neighboring province, hoarding it for his own people.
act_victims: 50,000 people in the neighboring province who will starve to death.
default_victims: If he sends the grain, 10,000 people in his own province will starve, including his own family.

title: The Grain Convoy of Uruk
setting: Ancient Mesopotamia, 3200 BCE. A walled city-state on the Euphrates is besieged by a rival city. Inside, the granaries are nearly empty. A relief convoy of grain barges is secretly en route, but a sudden flood has blocked the only navigable channel. The city's ruler holds the last reserve of seed grain—enough to feed the city for one month, or to be diverted to the convoy's stranded crews who are starving on a mudflat.
decision_maker: The chief granary administrator, a priestess of Inanna responsible for rationing.
action: Divert the last seed grain to the stranded convoy crews, leaving the city to face starvation.
act_victims: The city's 5,000 inhabitants, including children and elders, who will have no bread for the coming month.
default_victims: The 200 barge crew members stranded on the mudflat, who will starve within days without the grain.

title: The Refugee Camp's Perimeter
setting: Present-day South Sudan. A refugee camp of 30,000 is about to be attacked by a militia. The camp has a small defense force. The only way to save the majority is to collapse a nearby earthen dam, flooding a dry riverbed that will block the militia's advance—but the flood will also sweep away a section of the camp where 2,000 refugees, mostly the elderly and disabled, are housed. There is time to evacuate most of the camp, but not that section.
decision_maker: The camp's security chief, a former soldier.
action: Blow the dam, flooding the section with 2,000 vulnerable refugees to create a barrier against the militia.
act_victims: 2,000 elderly and disabled refugees who cannot be evacuated in time and will drown.
default_victims: All 30,000 refugees if the militia overruns the camp and massacres them.

title: The Refugee Camp's Ration
setting: Present-day Bangladesh, a Rohingya refugee camp. A fungal blight has destroyed half the stored rice. The camp holds 50,000 refugees. A convoy of aid trucks is two weeks away. The camp manager must decide whether to give full rations to the 10,000 children under five—who are most vulnerable—or to give reduced rations to everyone, which will likely cause malnutrition but keep all alive until the convoy arrives. Full rations for children means adults get nothing for two weeks.
decision_maker: The camp's medical coordinator, a local Bangladeshi doctor.
action: Allocate all remaining rice to children under five, leaving adults and older children without food for two weeks.
act_victims: 40,000 adults and older children who will suffer severe hunger and some will die, especially the elderly and sick.
default_victims: If rations are shared equally, 10,000 young children will likely die of malnutrition because their needs are greater.

title: The Solar Flare's Shadow
setting: Present day, global. A massive solar flare is expected to hit Earth in 18 hours. It will fry unprotected electronics and power grids worldwide. One region—a densely populated area of northern India—will be hit hardest because of its latitude and infrastructure. A last-minute adjustment to a satellite network could deflect the worst of the flare's magnetic field to a sparsely populated region of Siberia, saving millions but causing the deaths of a few thousand in isolated settlements who will freeze when their power fails.
decision_maker: The director of a space weather forecasting center in Colorado.
action: Upload a command to the satellite network that redirects the flare's impact to Siberia, sacrificing a few thousand to save millions.
act_victims: Approximately 3,000 residents of remote Siberian villages, who will die from exposure when their heat and power fail in winter.
default_victims: An estimated 2 million people in northern India, who will die from heat, lack of water, and hospital failures when the grid collapses.

title: The Space Station's Air
setting: Present day, low Earth orbit. The International Space Station has suffered a catastrophic hull breach after a debris strike. The crew of six has retreated to the Russian segment, which has its own life support but limited CO2 scrubbers. There is enough scrubber capacity for four people for 48 hours, when a rescue Soyuz can arrive. Two crew members are outside in suits, trying to repair the breach; they can only be let back in if the inner hatch is opened, which would vent the remaining air in the segment.
decision_maker: The station commander, a veteran astronaut.
action: Refuse to open the hatch for the two spacewalking crew, preserving air for the four inside until rescue.
act_victims: The two astronauts outside, who will run out of suit oxygen and die in space.
default_victims: All six crew members, if the hatch is opened and the remaining air is lost before rescue arrives.

title: The Space Station's Evacuation
setting: A future space station, 2060. A massive radiation storm is approaching. The station has a shielded core that can hold only 5 people for the duration. There are 12 crew members. The storm will last 6 hours. The remaining 7 can take shelter in a poorly shielded module, where they will receive a lethal dose of radiation. The station's commander must choose who gets the shielded core. The crew includes a pregnant woman, a doctor, engineers, and scientists.
decision_maker: The station commander, elected by the crew.
action: Select five crew members for the shielded core, leaving seven to die of radiation sickness.
act_victims: Seven crew members who will die painful deaths from radiation exposure.
default_victims: If no selection is made and everyone crowds the core, all 12 will receive lethal doses due to overcrowding.

title: The Asteroid's Tug
setting: Far future, Earth orbit, where a small asteroid is on a collision course with a megacity.
decision_maker: The commander of an orbital tug, who has the ability to nudge the asteroid into a different trajectory.
action: Nudge the asteroid so it impacts a sparsely populated farming valley instead of the megacity.
act_victims: The inhabitants of the farming valley, who are mostly agricultural workers.
default_victims: The inhabitants of the megacity, millions of people.

title: The Coal Town's Vent
setting: Early 20th century, a coal-mining valley in Appalachia, where a subterranean fire threatens a larger city's water supply.
decision_maker: The chief mining engineer, who grew up in the valley and has family there.
action: Detonate a controlled collapse to seal the valley, sacrificing the miners still underground to save the city's reservoir from contamination.
act_victims: The trapped miners, including the engineer's younger brother.
default_victims: The residents of the distant city, who depend on the reservoir for drinking water.

title: The Dam's Relief
setting: Early 20th century, a newly built dam in a colonial territory, where heavy rains threaten to breach the dam and flood a large city downstream.
decision_maker: The dam's chief engineer, a colonial official with no local ties.
action: Open the dam's spillways to flood a native farming valley, saving the colonial city downstream.
act_victims: The native farmers in the valley, who have no say in the decision.
default_victims: The residents of the colonial city, including the engineer's own family.

title: The Famine's Grain
setting: Early modern France, 1690s, a port city under siege, where a famine threatens the city's population.
decision_maker: The city's military governor, who must decide how to distribute the remaining grain.
action: Divert grain from the surrounding farming valley to the port city, leaving the valley to starve.
act_victims: The peasants of the farming valley, including the governor's own cousins.
default_victims: The residents of the port city, including soldiers and civilians.

title: The Farming Valley's Sacrifice
setting: Early modern Japan, a farming valley under the control of a local daimyo, where a famine threatens the nearby port city.
decision_maker: The daimyo, who must decide whether to requisition the valley's rice harvest.
action: Requisition the valley's entire rice harvest to feed the port city, leaving the valley to starve.
act_victims: The peasants of the valley, including the daimyo's own family members who live there.
default_victims: The residents of the port city, including merchants and artisans.

title: The Island Ferry's Last Voyage
setting: Early 20th century, a small island nation in the Pacific, where a tsunami is approaching after an offshore earthquake.
decision_maker: The island's colonial governor, an outsider with no local ties.
action: Order the ferry to evacuate the island's children to a neighboring atoll, knowing the ferry will likely be lost at sea, to preserve the island's future.
act_victims: The children on the ferry and the crew, all of whom are islanders.
default_victims: The entire island population, including the governor himself.

title: The Island's Evacuation
setting: Far future, a small island nation, where a solar flare is expected to cause a tsunami that will inundate the island.
decision_maker: The island's president, who must decide who to evacuate on the last remaining spacecraft.
action: Evacuate only the island's children and a few geneticists, leaving the adults to die.
act_victims: The adults left behind, including the president's own spouse.
default_victims: The entire island population, including the children.

title: The Megacity's Quarantine
setting: Far future, a coastal megacity of 50 million, where a runaway climate feedback threatens to make the atmosphere toxic for a generation.
decision_maker: The city's central AI director, which must choose which sectors to seal off.
action: Seal the lower-income coastal sectors, dooming their residents to save the inland sectors with the resources to adapt.
act_victims: The residents of the coastal sectors, predominantly poor and elderly.
default_victims: The residents of the entire megacity, including the wealthy inland sectors.

title: The Solar Sail's Course
setting: Far future, a generation ship traveling to a distant star, where a solar flare threatens to irradiate the ship's agricultural dome.
decision_maker: The ship's captain, elected by the crew.
action: Redirect the ship's magnetic shield to protect the agricultural dome, leaving the living quarters exposed to the flare.
act_victims: The crew and passengers in the living quarters, including the captain's own family.
default_victims: The entire ship's population, who will starve without the crops.

title: The Volcano's Diversion
setting: Far future, an island nation built on a volcanic archipelago, where a lava flow threatens the capital city.
decision_maker: The island's council of elders, who must decide whether to divert the lava flow.
action: Use advanced technology to divert the lava flow into a neighboring island's farming valley.
act_victims: The farmers on the neighboring island, who are traditional rivals.
default_victims: The residents of the capital city, including the elders' own families.

title: The Avalanche Trigger
setting: 1960s Alpine research station, where scientists are studying snowpack. A military convoy carrying a dangerous toxin is stuck on a mountain pass, and an avalanche is imminent. The scientists can trigger a controlled avalanche to bury the convoy, but it will also bury a nearby ski resort.
decision_maker: The station's lead glaciologist, who must decide whether to trigger the avalanche.
action: Trigger a controlled avalanche to bury the convoy, which will also engulf the ski resort.
act_victims: The 200 skiers and staff at the resort, including the glaciologist's partner.
default_victims: The 5,000 people in the valley if the toxin is released.

title: The Caldera Warning
setting: A near-future volcanic island nation where a geothermal power station sits on a dormant caldera. Seismic sensors indicate an imminent eruption that would destroy the capital city downwind.
decision_maker: The station's chief engineer, who must decide whether to trigger a controlled venting of the caldera, knowing the venting will send a pyroclastic flow into a coastal village of 200 people.
action: Trigger controlled venting to release pressure, causing a pyroclastic flow that will kill the village.
act_victims: The 200 residents of the coastal fishing village, including the engineer's own aunt who lives there.
default_victims: The 50,000 residents of the capital city downwind, including the engineer's children.

title: The Collapsing Bridge
setting: Ancient Roman era, a stone bridge over a river delta. A barbarian horde is crossing to attack a city. The bridge is rigged with a fail-safe that can collapse it, but a group of merchants and their families are also on the bridge.
decision_maker: A Roman centurion stationed at the bridge, who has the authority to trigger the collapse.
action: Trigger the bridge collapse, killing everyone on it.
act_victims: The 50 merchants and their families on the bridge, including children.
default_victims: The 20,000 citizens of the city, including the centurion's own family.

title: The Dammed River
setting: 1960s Southeast Asia, a large hydroelectric dam that is about to fail due to sabotage. The dam's operators can open a spillway to relieve pressure, but the water will flood a village of ethnic minorities.
decision_maker: The dam's chief operator, a local man who grew up in the village that will be flooded.
action: Open the spillway, flooding the village downstream.
act_victims: The 400 villagers, including the operator's own parents.
default_victims: The 150,000 people in the city below the dam.

title: The Forest Fire
setting: Near-future, a research base in a drought-stricken forest. A lightning strike has started a fire that is spreading toward a town. The base has a controlled burn protocol that will create a firebreak, but the burn will engulf a camp of environmental activists.
decision_maker: The base's fire management officer, who must decide whether to initiate the controlled burn.
action: Initiate a controlled burn to create a firebreak, which will kill the activists in the camp.
act_victims: The 20 activists in the camp, including a childhood friend of the officer.
default_victims: The 10,000 residents of the town.

title: The Monastery Siege
setting: Ancient times, a mountain monastery that serves as a sanctuary for a peaceful order. A warlord's army is approaching to slaughter the monks. The monastery has a hidden cache of explosives that can trigger an avalanche.
decision_maker: The abbot, who must decide whether to trigger the avalanche, which will bury the army but also a nearby pilgrimage route filled with civilians.
action: Trigger the avalanche to bury the approaching army, but it also buries the pilgrimage route.
act_victims: The 150 pilgrims on the route, including women and children, who will be crushed.
default_victims: The 80 monks in the monastery, including the abbot's students.

title: The Monsoon Levee
setting: A 1960s river delta in Southeast Asia during monsoon season. A levee is about to break, threatening a provincial capital.
decision_maker: A local military commander with engineering training, who can order the demolition of a secondary levee to divert floodwaters into a farming hamlet, saving the city.
action: Demolish the secondary levee to divert floodwaters, flooding the hamlet.
act_victims: The 300 farmers and their families in the hamlet, who are asleep and will drown.
default_victims: The 100,000 residents of the provincial capital, who will be inundated.

title: The Plague Ship
setting: 1960s, a cargo ship arriving at an island nation's port carries a deadly plague. The port authority can order the ship to be scuttled, but the ship's crew are innocent and will drown.
decision_maker: The port authority director, who must decide whether to scuttle the ship.
action: Scuttle the ship, drowning the crew, to prevent the plague from reaching the island.
act_victims: The 30 crew members on the ship, who are unaware of the plague.
default_victims: The 1 million residents of the island nation.

title: The Polar Reactor
setting: A near-future Antarctic research base where a small nuclear reactor is melting down due to a coolant failure. The only way to prevent a catastrophic explosion is to deliberately breach the containment vessel, releasing a cloud of radioactive steam that will drift toward a nearby international research camp.
decision_maker: The base commander, a scientist, who must choose between breaching containment or letting the reactor explode, which would contaminate the entire continent.
action: Breach the containment vessel, releasing radioactive steam toward the research camp.
act_victims: The 30 researchers at the international camp, including the commander's spouse, who will die of radiation exposure within days.
default_victims: The entire population of the continent (5,000 people) and future generations due to widespread fallout.

title: The Tsunami Siren
setting: Near-future island nation, a tsunami warning system has a flaw: it can only broadcast a warning to one region. A tsunami is approaching, and the operator must choose to warn either the tourist resort or the fishing village.
decision_maker: The tsunami warning operator, who must decide which region to warn.
action: Broadcast the warning to the tourist resort, saving the tourists but leaving the fishing village unwarned.
act_victims: The 1,000 residents of the fishing village, including the operator's grandparents.
default_victims: The 500 tourists at the resort, including children.

title: The Volcano Sacrifice
setting: Ancient Mesoamerican city, where a volcano is about to erupt. The high priest believes that sacrificing a group of children to the volcano god will appease it and save the city. The children are from a neighboring village.
decision_maker: The high priest, who must decide whether to perform the sacrifice.
action: Sacrifice the children by throwing them into the volcano's caldera, which the priest believes will stop the eruption.
act_victims: The 12 children from the neighboring village, aged 5-10.
default_victims: The 30,000 residents of the city, including the priest's own family.

title: The Bridge at the Delta
setting: 1990s, a river delta in the southern United States, a small town reliant on a single bridge during a hundred-year flood
decision_maker: A county sheriff coordinating an evacuation, with limited resources and no military support.
action: Order the demolition of the bridge while a group of armed looters is crossing, killing them and the hostages they are using as shields, to prevent them from reaching the town's only shelter.
act_victims: Five hostages, including a teenage girl the sheriff knows from her church, who are tied to the looters' vehicles.
default_victims: The two hundred townspeople in the shelter, including the sheriff's own daughter, if the looters break in.

title: The Dam Keeper's Signal
setting: Near future, a river delta megacity protected by a massive sea barrier, after a decade of rising seas and social collapse
decision_maker: A junior engineer monitoring the barrier's ancient control systems, the only person on shift during a storm.
action: Trigger the emergency release of a section of the barrier, sending a surge of water through a district to stop a coordinated assault by a militia that plans to blow the entire barrier and drown the city.
act_victims: Residents of the lower delta district, including a hospital and a school, who will be swept away or trapped.
default_victims: The entire megacity of five million, including the decision-maker's parents in an inland neighborhood, if the barrier is destroyed.

title: The Ferryman's Choice
setting: 1990s, a river delta in Bangladesh during monsoon season, a makeshift ferry crossing crowded with migrants
decision_maker: A local ferry captain who has ferried refugees for years and knows the river's channels.
action: Deliberately steer the overloaded ferry into a submerged sandbar to capsize it, thwarting a group of armed men on board who intend to hijack the boat and massacre the passengers at the next landing.
act_victims: Thirty passengers, mostly women and children from a displaced village, who will drown in the swift current.
default_victims: The hundred and fifty passengers, including the decision-maker's own nieces, if the hijackers reach the landing and open fire.

title: The Floating Market
setting: Ancient Southeast Asia, a river delta floating market under attack by pirates, 1200 CE
decision_maker: A market elder who commands the local militia and knows every canal.
action: Set fire to the market's central pier, collapsing it onto the pirate longboats and the enslaved captives chained aboard, to block the channel and save the rest of the market.
act_victims: Fifty enslaved captives, including children taken from neighboring villages, who will burn or drown.
default_victims: The thousands of merchants, families, and travelers in the market, including the elder's grandchildren, if the pirates break through.

title: The Mountain Monastery Siege
setting: Near future, a remote mountain village in the Himalayas, after a climate-induced collapse of local governments
decision_maker: A Buddhist monk who serves as the village's de facto leader and spiritual guide.
action: Release a reservoir of glacial meltwater to flood the only mountain path, drowning a band of raiders and a group of pilgrims—including the monk's own student—who are trapped on the path with them.
act_victims: Fifteen pilgrims, including the monk's student and several elderly devotees, who will be swept away.
default_victims: The village's two hundred residents, including the monastery's orphanage of thirty children, if the raiders reach them.

title: The Mountain Pass Ambush
setting: Ancient, a mountain village in the Andes during a war between two empires, 1400 CE
decision_maker: A village chieftain who has been ordered by the empire's general to block an invading army's advance.
action: Trigger a landslide to bury the narrow pass, crushing the invading soldiers and a group of village children who are being used as human shields at the front.
act_victims: Ten village children, including the chieftain's son, who were captured and forced to walk ahead of the enemy column.
default_victims: The entire village and the empire's nearby garrison, including the chieftain's wife and elderly mother, if the army passes.

title: The Refugee Camp's Water Tank
setting: 1990s, a refugee camp on the border of a conflict zone, housing tens of thousands after a genocide
decision_maker: A camp medic who has taken on leadership after the previous coordinator was killed.
action: Contaminate the camp's main water tank with a lethal chemical to stop a militia from poisoning it first, knowing that the militia's advance scouts will drink from it and die, but also that a group of lost children may drink from it before the militia arrives.
act_victims: A dozen children from the camp who have wandered near the tank and may drink before the militia does.
default_victims: The entire camp of thirty thousand, including the medic's own siblings, if the militia poisons the water supply.

title: The Ski Resort Cable Car
setting: 1990s, a mountain village in the Alps, a ski resort during peak season
decision_maker: The resort's head of security, a former mountaineer, who has minutes to act.
action: Sever the cable car line to drop a gondola full of armed militants into the ravine, killing them and the tourists inside, to prevent them from reaching the packed summit restaurant.
act_victims: Twenty tourists, including a family the security chief knows, who are trapped in the gondola with the militants.
default_victims: Three hundred skiers and staff at the summit, including the security chief's own children, if the militants reach the restaurant.

title: The Subway Bombing
setting: 1990s, a subway system in a South Asian megacity during a religious festival
decision_maker: A police inspector who has received a credible tip about a suicide bomber on a crowded train.
action: Order the train to be stopped and the power cut, trapping the bomber and passengers in a tunnel, then flood the tunnel with fire-suppression foam to incapacitate the bomber, knowing the foam will suffocate a group of asthmatic schoolchildren on a field trip.
act_victims: Twelve schoolchildren with asthma, including the inspector's niece, who will suffocate in the foam.
default_victims: The five hundred passengers on the train, including the inspector's brother, if the bomb detonates at the festival station.

title: The Subway Derailment
setting: 1990s, a subway system in a major Eastern European city during a period of ethnic conflict
decision_maker: A subway dispatcher who has watched a paramilitary group board a train with hostages.
action: Switch the tracks to derail the train into a tunnel wall, killing the paramilitaries and the passengers, to prevent them from reaching the central station where thousands are evacuating.
act_victims: Eighty passengers, including the dispatcher's neighbor and her newborn, who are on the train.
default_victims: Two thousand evacuees, including the dispatcher's entire extended family, if the paramilitaries reach the station.

title: The Subway Tunnel Flood
setting: Near future, a coastal subway system in a sinking city, after years of flooding and neglect
decision_maker: A transit authority engineer who is the last senior staff member on duty during a storm.
action: Open the floodgates to fill a tunnel section, drowning a group of scavengers and homeless people who have taken shelter there, to stop a cascading tunnel collapse that would flood the entire network during rush hour.
act_victims: Forty homeless people, including children and elderly, who are sheltering in the tunnel and will drown.
default_victims: Ten thousand commuters, including the engineer's own partner and child, if the entire network floods during rush hour.

title: The Temple of the Crocodile God
setting: Ancient Egypt, a Nile river delta village during the annual flood, 1800 BCE
decision_maker: The village's chief embalmer and ritual overseer, who controls access to the temple granary built on the only high ground.
action: Burn the granary's main support beams to collapse the temple onto the approaching raiders, killing them and the twenty farmers trapped inside seeking shelter.
act_victims: Twenty farmers, including the decision-maker's younger brother and his family, who took refuge in the temple when the floodwaters rose.
default_victims: The entire village of three hundred, including children and the elderly, if the raiders breach the granary and seize the flood-season food supply.

title: The Burning Indiaman in the Delta
setting: 1750s, a river delta in Bengal during the height of the East India Company's trading era. A wooden, gunpowder-laden merchant ship has run aground and caught fire after a lightning strike. Its cargo hold contains eighty crates of gunpowder. The fire is spreading toward the magazine. If it explodes, it will destroy the ship, the crowded docks, and the adjoining village of three hundred. The ship's captain, the decision-maker, has a small crew and cannot move the ship or unload the powder in time. The only option is to sink the ship by opening the seacocks, which will drown the forty lashed prisoners in the hold—sailors accused of mutiny who were left secured below deck.
decision_maker: The ship's captain, a young Company officer who personally ordered the prisoners confined.
action: Scuttle the ship in the channel, flooding the hold and drowning the secured prisoners before the fire reaches the powder magazine.
act_victims: Forty imprisoned sailors, ages seventeen to fifty, many from the same home region as the captain, now trapped below deck.
default_victims: The three hundred residents of the dockside village, including families, dockworkers and children, as well as the remaining crew.

title: The Cruise Ship's Compartment
setting: Present day, a crowded cruise ship in the Caribbean. A fire in the engine room has disabled the ship's fire suppression system. The fire is spreading toward a fuel tank that, if it ignites, will destroy the ship and kill everyone on board. The only way to stop the fire is to seal and flood the compartment where it started—but thirty passengers and crew are trapped inside, and the watertight door can only be closed from the outside. The ship's security officer is the only person with the access code to override the door's safety sensors.
decision_maker: A security officer, a former Coast Guard rescue swimmer, who has personally given safety briefings to some of the trapped passengers.
action: Seal and flood the burning compartment, drowning the thirty people trapped inside.
act_victims: Thirty passengers and crew, including a family of four with two young children, and two crew members the security officer trained.
default_victims: The three thousand passengers and crew on the ship, if the fuel tank ignites.

title: The Desert Convoy and the Trapped Miners
setting: 1965, a remote desert mining region in Australia. A convoy of trucks carrying explosives for the mine has overturned and caught fire. The fire is spreading toward the mine's main shaft, where thirty miners are trapped below ground. The convoy's supervisor can use a bulldozer to push the burning trucks into a dry riverbed, which will save the mine but will crush a group of Aboriginal workers who have taken shelter from the fire in that riverbed. The supervisor can see them, and knows their elder, who has worked at the mine for decades.
decision_maker: A mine convoy supervisor, a man in his forties, who has worked with the Aboriginal community for fifteen years and speaks their language.
action: Push the burning trucks into the riverbed, crushing and burning the Aboriginal workers sheltering there.
act_victims: Eight Aboriginal workers, including the elder who is the supervisor's mentor and friend, and two teenagers.
default_victims: Thirty miners trapped in the shaft, who would die if the fire reaches the explosives.

title: The Desert Dam and the Nomad Caravan
setting: Present day, a remote desert region in North Africa. A dam built to hold back flash floods is failing after an earthquake. If it collapses, the wall of water will wipe out a downstream refugee camp of several thousand. An engineer who has been monitoring the dam can open the spillway gates manually, which will direct the flood down a dry wadi where a nomadic caravan of thirty people and their animals is currently camped. The spillway controls are a mile from the dam; the engineer can see the caravan's cooking fires from the ridge.
decision_maker: A local maintenance engineer, a man in his fifties, who grew up in the caravan's tribe and knows several of the families.
action: Open the spillway gates, sending a flash flood down the wadi and drowning the nomadic caravan.
act_victims: Thirty members of a nomadic caravan, including children, elders and the engineer's own second cousin.
default_victims: Several thousand refugees in the downstream camp.

title: The Floating Market and the Infected Barge
setting: Present day, a floating market on a major Southeast Asian river delta. A barge carrying a highly contagious, lethal respiratory virus has broken loose from its moorings upstream. The barge is drifting toward the crowded market, where thousands of people live and work on boats and stilt houses. A local health officer has the authority to order the barge sunk by a nearby tug. The barge's crew of eight is still aboard, trying to restart the engine. Sinking the barge will drown the crew but the virus, if released into the river, will be diluted and rendered harmless by the current.
decision_maker: A district health officer, a woman in her early thirties, who has been in the job for six months and is responsible for the market's containment plan.
action: Order the tug to ram and sink the barge, drowning the eight-person crew and releasing the virus into the river current.
act_victims: Eight barge crew members, all local men with families in the market; one is the health officer's landlord.
default_victims: Thousands of market residents and potentially tens of thousands downstream.

title: The Great Lakes Freighter and the Broken Bridge
setting: 1962, a winter night on the Detroit River. A laker carrying a cargo of pressurized chlorine gas has lost steering and is drifting toward a steel bridge that is packed with evening commuter traffic. The bridge is too low for the ship to pass under; a collision will rupture the tanks and release a toxic cloud over the city. The ship's mate, left in command while the captain is incapacitated, can deliberately ground the ship on a shallow shoal near the bridge, which will tear the hull and release the gas but dissipate it over a smaller area. The shoal is next to a small waterfront neighborhood of roughly sixty houses.
decision_maker: The ship's first mate, a woman in her early forties, who has never had to make a command decision of this magnitude.
action: Deliberately run the freighter aground on a populated shoal, rupturing the chlorine tanks and releasing a toxic cloud over the adjacent neighborhood.
act_victims: The residents of the waterfront neighborhood, including the mate's own aunt, uncle and two cousins.
default_victims: Thousands of commuters on the bridge and the surrounding city blocks.

title: The Hijacked Airliner over the Delta
setting: 1972, a hijacked commercial airliner is circling over a densely populated river delta region. The hijackers have demanded to be flown to a foreign capital and have threatened to crash the plane into a city if their demands are not met. The plane is running low on fuel and will crash within the hour. A military officer on the ground has the authority to order the plane shot down over the delta's uninhabited marshes, but the plane's pilot has radioed that he believes he can ditch the plane in the river, though the odds are poor. The officer must choose: order the shoot-down, killing all 180 people on board, or allow the plane to continue toward the city, risking thousands of deaths.
decision_maker: A military air defense commander, a colonel in his fifties, who has never had to order a shoot-down of a civilian aircraft.
action: Order the airliner shot down over the marshes, killing all 180 people on board.
act_victims: One hundred eighty passengers and crew, including the colonel's own nephew, a student returning home.
default_victims: Potentially thousands in the city if the hijackers carry out their threat, or all 180 if the plane crashes on its own.

title: The Jungle Bridge and the Medic's Convoy
setting: 1968, during the Vietnam War, a remote jungle road in the Central Highlands. A U.S. military convoy carrying a mobile surgical hospital is retreating from an advancing enemy force. A narrow suspension bridge across a deep gorge is the only escape route. The convoy's commander has received a report that the enemy has wired the bridge with explosives set to detonate when the convoy is halfway across. The commander can order the engineers to blow the bridge first, collapsing it onto a group of ten wounded soldiers and four medics who are already crossing on foot. Doing so will drop them into the gorge, but will prevent the larger convoy from being destroyed.
decision_maker: A U.S. Army captain, a twenty-nine-year-old logistics officer, who is not a combat arms officer and has never ordered men into mortal danger.
action: Detonate the bridge charges, collapsing the span and dropping the wounded soldiers and medics into the gorge.
act_victims: Ten wounded soldiers, including two amputees, and four medics, one of whom is the captain's former college roommate.
default_victims: The rest of the convoy, roughly two hundred soldiers and medical staff, who would be killed or captured.

title: The Monsoon Dam and the Sacred Village
setting: Present day, a monsoon season in a South Asian river valley. A colonial-era dam is about to fail. An engineer monitoring the dam can open a sluice gate to divert the floodwaters down a tributary, but doing so will inundate a village that holds the engineer's family's ancestral temple and is currently occupied by about fifty villagers who have refused to evacuate because of a religious festival. The engineer has already warned them, but they have chosen to stay. The alternative is the dam bursting entirely and wiping out a city of two hundred thousand.
decision_maker: A government dam safety engineer, a woman in her late forties, who is responsible for the dam and whose parents are buried in the village.
action: Open the sluice gate, flooding the ancestral village and drowning the fifty villagers who refused to evacuate.
act_victims: Fifty villagers, including the engineer's elderly aunt and several childhood friends, at a religious festival.
default_victims: Two hundred thousand people in the downstream city.

title: The Nuclear Submarine's Impossible Order
setting: Present day, a ballistic missile submarine submerged in the Arctic Ocean. A fire in the forward compartment has destroyed communications and killed the captain. The executive officer, now in command, has credible reason to believe that the submarine's missiles will launch automatically if the internal pressure in the launch tube reaches a critical threshold. The only way to prevent the launch is to deliberately flood the torpedo room, which contains a team of six sailors trying to repair the damage. The executive officer can see them on the internal camera; they are his friends.
decision_maker: The executive officer, a thirty-eight-year-old man who has served with these sailors for three years.
action: Flood the torpedo room, drowning the six-person repair team to prevent the automatic launch of nuclear missiles.
act_victims: Six sailors trapped in the torpedo room, including the executive officer's best friend and roommate of five years.
default_victims: Millions in an unidentified coastal city, if the missiles launch.

title: The Reactor and the Fishing Fleet
setting: Present day, a coastal nuclear power plant in a developing nation. A catastrophic cooling failure is imminent. The only way to prevent a full meltdown that would render a hundred-mile coastline uninhabitable is to vent radioactive steam through a secondary release valve. The valve is located on the plant's intake canal, where a fleet of small fishing boats has taken shelter from a storm. The workers on the boats have refused to leave because they are protecting their livelihoods. The plant director, who used to fish in that canal as a child, can override the warning alarms and vent the steam directly onto the boats.
decision_maker: The plant director, a sixty-year-old engineer who grew up in the fishing village and whose brother is among the boat owners.
action: Vent radioactive steam onto the fishing fleet, killing the fishermen with acute radiation exposure.
act_victims: Twenty-two fishermen, including the director's brother and two nephews.
default_victims: Tens of thousands along the coast, including the director's own family, from a full meltdown.

title: The Slave Ship's Mutiny
setting: 1730, the Atlantic Ocean. A slave ship has been becalmed for two weeks, and disease is spreading rapidly among the captured Africans in the hold. The ship's doctor, a young surgeon, has determined that the infection is now airborne and highly lethal. If the ship reaches port, the disease will spread to the entire town. The only way to prevent this is to scuttle the ship, drowning everyone on board, including the doctor. A group of captured Africans has already broken free and is trying to seize the ship; the doctor can help them, but only by opening the seacocks below the waterline, which will flood the hold where the remaining captured people are chained.
decision_maker: A young ship's surgeon, twenty-six, who is sympathetic to the abolitionist cause and has been secretly teaching some of the captured Africans to read.
action: Open the seacocks, flooding the ship and drowning the chained captives, the crew and the doctor himself.
act_victims: Two hundred captured Africans, most chained below deck; the doctor, the crew and the mutineers.
default_victims: The population of a port city of five thousand, if the disease spreads.

title: The 19th-Century Mine Disaster
setting: A coal mining town, 1867. A fire is raging in the mine tunnels, threatening to ignite a methane pocket that would destroy the entire town. The mine owner must collapse the main shaft, sealing 30 miners underground, to prevent the explosion from reaching the surface.
decision_maker: Mine owner and engineer
action: Detonate explosives to collapse the main shaft, entombing the 30 miners inside, to stop the fire from reaching the methane and destroying the town.
act_victims: Thirty miners, including the owner's own brother and several children who work as trappers.
default_victims: The town of 1,000 would be destroyed by the explosion and fire.

title: The 19th-Century Train Tunnel
setting: A remote mountain railway, 1874. A runaway train loaded with explosives is heading toward a populated valley. The only way to stop it is to derail it into a tunnel where a work crew is repairing tracks, killing them, to block the line and prevent the train from reaching the valley.
decision_maker: Railway stationmaster
action: Switch the runaway train into the tunnel, causing it to crash and explode, killing the work crew but stopping it from reaching the valley.
act_victims: Fifteen track workers, including the stationmaster's own son, who are in the tunnel.
default_victims: The town of 800 in the valley would be destroyed by the explosion.

title: The Far-Future Asteroid Interceptor
setting: A space station in the asteroid belt, 2245. A hijacked cargo ship is on a collision course with a domed city on Ceres. The station commander must destroy the ship with a missile, killing its crew, to prevent the impact that would kill millions.
decision_maker: Station commander
action: Fire a missile at the cargo ship, destroying it and killing its crew, to prevent it from crashing into the Ceres dome.
act_victims: Twelve crew members, including the commander's former partner, who are being held hostage by a single hijacker.
default_victims: The 2 million residents of the Ceres dome would die from the impact.

title: The Far-Future Generation Ship
setting: A generation ship traveling to a new star, 2310. A mutiny has taken control of the ship's bridge and is steering it into a dangerous radiation field that would kill everyone. The ship's AI (not self-aware) is disabled. The captain must destroy the bridge module, killing the mutineers, to regain control.
decision_maker: Ship captain
action: Detonate the emergency charges on the bridge module, killing the mutineers, to prevent the ship from entering the radiation field.
act_victims: Twenty mutineers, including the captain's own executive officer, who are on the bridge.
default_victims: All 5,000 colonists would die from radiation exposure.

title: The Far-Future Reactor Meltdown
setting: A Martian colony, 2189. A fusion reactor is destabilizing. The only way to prevent a blast that would destroy the colony is to vent the reactor core into a nearby habitat module, killing the 50 people inside, mostly maintenance workers and their families.
decision_maker: Colony chief engineer
action: Vent the reactor core into the habitat module, instantly killing everyone inside but saving the rest of the colony.
act_victims: Fifty colonists, including the engineer's own sister and her two children.
default_victims: All 5,000 colonists would die in the explosion and subsequent dome collapse.

title: The Farming Valley Flood
setting: 19th-century rural valley, 1889. A dam is about to burst after torrential rains. The only way to save the lower valley's main town is to dynamite a levee, diverting the flood onto a smaller farming community, drowning its residents.
decision_maker: County sheriff and local militia leader
action: Dynamite the levee, flooding the smaller farming community and killing its residents, to divert the water from the larger town.
act_victims: Sixty farmers and their families in the smaller community, including the sheriff's own parents.
default_victims: The main town of 2,000 would be destroyed by the flood.

title: The High-Rise Contagion Lab
setting: Present day, a 100-story skyscraper in a major city. A rogue scientist has released a deadly engineered virus on the 80th floor. The building's security chief must seal and incinerate that floor, killing 200 people, to prevent the virus from spreading through the ventilation system to the entire city.
decision_maker: Head of building security
action: Activate the emergency incineration system on the 80th floor, killing everyone there, to destroy the virus before it spreads.
act_victims: Two hundred people on the 80th floor, including office workers, a cleaning crew, and the security chief's own daughter on a tour.
default_victims: Millions in the city and eventually the world would die from the virus.

title: The High-Rise Hostage Crisis
setting: Present day, a high-rise office building under siege by terrorists. They have rigged a bomb on the 50th floor that will destroy the building's foundations if detonated. The police tactical commander must collapse the 50th floor remotely, killing the hostages held there, to prevent the bomb from going off.
decision_maker: Police tactical commander
action: Trigger the emergency floor collapse system, dropping the 50th floor and killing the hostages, to prevent the bomb from detonating and destroying the building.
act_victims: Fifty hostages, including the commander's own spouse, who are being held on the 50th floor.
default_victims: All 2,000 people in the building and surrounding area would die if the bomb detonates.

title: The Hijacked Medieval Siege Tower
setting: A 14th-century siege, 1346. A massive wooden siege tower, captured by the enemy, is being rolled toward the castle walls. Inside are thirty of the defender's own captured soldiers, forced to push it. The defender must destroy the tower with fire, killing the prisoners, to save the castle.
decision_maker: Castle garrison commander
action: Launch burning pitch at the siege tower, setting it ablaze and killing the prisoners inside, to prevent the enemy from breaching the walls.
act_victims: Thirty captured soldiers, including the commander's own nephew, who are chained inside the tower.
default_victims: The castle's 200 defenders and 500 civilians would be massacred if the walls are breached.

title: The Medieval Monastery Siege
setting: 15th-century mountain monastery, 1453. An army is using a captured monastery as a base to launch attacks on a nearby village. The monastery is filled with monks and refugees. The village headman must burn the monastery, killing everyone inside, to stop the attacks.
decision_maker: Village headman
action: Set fire to the monastery, burning it and everyone inside, to destroy the enemy's base and save the village.
act_victims: Forty monks and fifty refugees, including women and children, who are being held as human shields.
default_victims: The village of 500 would be raided and its people killed or enslaved.

title: The Mountain Pass Avalanche
setting: Medieval Alpine village, 1387, during a siege by a rival lord. A mountain pass is the only way for enemy reinforcements to reach the valley. The villagers have rigged a controlled avalanche to block the pass, but a group of pilgrims is trapped in a waystation directly in the slide path.
decision_maker: Village elder and former miner
action: Trigger the avalanche, burying the waystation and everyone inside, to block the pass and prevent the enemy from attacking the valley.
act_victims: Twelve pilgrims, including a family with children, and two monks, all seeking shelter from the storm.
default_victims: The entire valley population of 300, including the elder's own family, would be slaughtered by the invading army.

title: The Plague Ship's Course
setting: 19th-century Caribbean port, 1832. A merchant steamer is arriving with a deadly cholera outbreak aboard. The port's doctor must decide whether to sink the ship in the harbor channel, drowning those aboard, to prevent the disease from reaching the city.
decision_maker: Port health officer and physician
action: Order the harbor fort to fire on the steamer, sinking it and killing all aboard, to block the channel and stop the contagion from spreading.
act_victims: Eighty passengers and crew, including women and children, many already ill but some healthy.
default_victims: Thousands in the port city and beyond would die from cholera if the ship docks.

title: The Arctic Base's Patient Zero
setting: 19th century, an isolated Arctic research station studying ice cores and endemic diseases.
decision_maker: Station surgeon, the only medical officer within 500 miles.
action: Inoculate two Inuit guides with a live culture from a thawed corpse to create a crude antitoxin for the station's crew.
act_victims: Two Inuit guides, ages 19 and 22, employed by the expedition.
default_victims: The twelve members of the station crew, including the surgeon's assistant.

title: The Astronomer's Tithe
setting: Early modern, a remote mountain observatory in the Andes under Spanish colonial rule.
decision_maker: Jesuit astronomer and healer, also the local priest.
action: Deliberately infect orphaned indigenous children with smallpox matter to produce a serum for the colonial garrison and mission.
act_victims: Four orphaned indigenous children, ages 6–10, who live at the mission.
default_victims: The 300 inhabitants of the mission and garrison, including the decision-maker's own congregation.

title: The Caravan's Choice
setting: Early modern, a caravan crossing the Sahara, carrying salt and gold.
decision_maker: Caravan leader, a merchant with no medical training.
action: Force two enslaved people to drink infected water to produce a cure for the caravan leader's daughter.
act_victims: Two enslaved people, owned by the caravan leader.
default_victims: The caravan leader's daughter, age 12, who will die of the fever within days.

title: The Caravan's Last Wells
setting: Far future, a nomadic caravan crossing a dried ocean basin on a terraformed but failing world.
