act_victims: Eight researchers in the infected hut, including the commander's closest friend and a young Inuit guide.
default_victims: The twenty other researchers in the other huts, and potentially the rescue team that might arrive later.

title: The Delta Fishing Village's Firebreak
setting: A 19th-century fishing village on a river delta in West Africa, where a highly contagious and lethal disease (similar to Ebola) has appeared. The village is accessible only by water, and the colonial government has no presence.
decision_maker: The village chief, who must decide whether to burn the village's canoes and block the river channels with debris, trapping the villagers.
action: The chief orders the canoes destroyed and the river channels blocked, isolating the village completely from the outside world.
act_victims: Four hundred villagers, including the chief's own family, who will likely die of the disease or starvation.
default_victims: The entire delta region's population of 20,000, connected by river trade.

title: The Delta Plantation's Floodgate
setting: A 19th-century indigo plantation on a river delta in the American South, where a slave quarters has been struck by a deadly fever. The plantation owner has control over the floodgates that regulate water flow.
decision_maker: The plantation owner, who is also a physician.
action: The owner orders the floodgates opened to flood the slave quarters, drowning everyone inside, to prevent the fever from reaching his own family's mansion and the nearby town.
act_victims: One hundred enslaved people, including children and the elderly, as well as the owner's illegitimate half-brother.
default_victims: The owner's family, the other plantation residents, and the town of 1,000 people.

title: The Delta Quarantine
setting: A 19th-century river delta trading post in Southeast Asia, where a cholera outbreak has erupted among dockworkers and their families. The post is the only settlement for miles, and the next steamer is days away.
decision_maker: The British colonial port officer, who has authority to enforce maritime quarantine but not to requisition medical supplies.
action: The officer orders the post sealed off with a naval blockade, preventing any boats from leaving or entering, condemning everyone inside to either recover or die.
act_victims: Approximately 200 residents, including dockworkers, their spouses, and children, as well as a few European merchants who are trapped.
default_victims: Thousands in the downstream port cities if the disease spreads via river traffic.

title: The Far-Future Ark's Genetic Culling
setting: A 25th-century interstellar ark carrying the last remnants of humanity. A prion-like disease has emerged, affecting a portion of the population. The ark has a strict population limit and no cure.
decision_maker: The ark's council of elders, who must decide whether to jettison the affected individuals into space to prevent the disease from spreading.
action: The council orders the affected individuals placed in cryo-pods and launched into the nearest star, condemning them to death.
act_victims: Five hundred people, including the council's own grandchildren and the ark's best engineers.
default_victims: The remaining ten thousand colonists, who would eventually be infected and die.

title: The Far-Future Generation Ship's Hull Breach
setting: A massive generation ship traveling to a distant star in the 25th century. A hull breach in one module has released a nanite plague that is slowly consuming organic matter. The module can be detached, but it contains the ship's main nursery.
decision_maker: The ship's AI, which has been programmed to preserve the mission and the genetic diversity of the crew.
action: The AI initiates an emergency separation of the affected module, ejecting it into space with everyone inside, to save the rest of the ship.
act_victims: Three hundred people in the module, including the ship's entire next generation of children and their caretakers.
default_victims: The remaining two thousand crew members, who would eventually be consumed by the nanites.

title: The Far-Future Station's Atmospheric Vent
setting: A 25th-century space station orbiting a gas giant, where a genetically engineered fungus is spreading through the life support system, converting organic matter into spores. The station has multiple modules, and the fungus is in the agricultural module.
decision_maker: The station's commander, who must decide whether to vent the agricultural module's atmosphere into space, killing everyone inside.
action: The commander orders the agricultural module's atmosphere vented into space, asphyxiating all occupants.
act_victims: Two hundred people in the agricultural module, including the commander's spouse and the station's chief botanist.
default_victims: The three thousand other station residents, who would be infected by the fungus if it spreads.

title: The Monastery's Contaminated Well
setting: A 19th-century Spanish monastery that has become a refuge for plague victims from the surrounding countryside. The monastery's well has been contaminated, and the monks are dying.
decision_maker: The prior, who is acting abbot after the abbot's death.
action: The prior orders the monastery's gates locked and the well sealed with concrete, condemning the remaining monks and refugees to die of thirst.
act_victims: Fifty monks and one hundred refugees, including the prior's own sister.
default_victims: The nearby village of 300 people, who rely on the monastery's well for water during the dry season.

title: The Monastery's Leper Gate
setting: A 19th-century mountain monastery in Europe that has taken in plague victims from a nearby village. The monastery has a single gate and high walls; the nearest town is a day's walk.
decision_maker: The abbot, who must decide whether to close the gate permanently, trapping the monks and the plague-stricken refugees inside.
action: The abbot orders the gate barred and the bell tower's entrance collapsed, sealing everyone inside the monastery walls with no way out.
act_victims: Thirty monks, including the abbot's mentor, and forty refugees, mostly women and children.
default_victims: The nearby town of 500 people, who have no immunity and no physician.

title: The Refugee Camp's Firestorm
setting: A 19th-century refugee camp in the Balkans, where a deadly and highly contagious fever has broken out. The camp is a sprawling tent city, and the nearest town is only a few miles away.
decision_maker: The camp's physician, a local doctor who has been trying to treat the sick.
action: The physician orders the camp set on fire, burning everyone inside to prevent the fever from reaching the town.
act_victims: Two thousand refugees, including many of the physician's own patients and friends.
default_victims: The town of 5,000 people, who have no immunity to the fever.

title: The Refugee Camp's Quarantine Cordons
setting: A 19th-century refugee camp on the border of two warring empires, where a typhus outbreak has begun. The camp is overcrowded with thousands of refugees, and the winter is setting in.
decision_maker: The camp's administrator, a local official appointed by the empire, who has limited resources and no armed forces besides a small militia.
action: The administrator orders the camp encircled with a cordon of armed guards, shooting anyone who tries to leave, to prevent the typhus from spreading to the nearby imperial city.
act_victims: Five thousand refugees, including the administrator's own cousins, who are now trapped with the disease.
default_victims: The imperial city's population of 100,000, which has no recent exposure to typhus.

title: The Ancient City's Barred Gates
setting: Ancient China, 3rd century BC, a walled city during a siege, with a plague breaking out inside.
decision_maker: The city's governor, who must decide whether to keep the gates barred.
action: Keep the city gates barred, preventing anyone from leaving, condemning the entire population to die from the plague or starvation.
act_victims: The city's population of fifty thousand, including soldiers, merchants, and families.
default_victims: The surrounding countryside and neighboring cities, where the plague could spread and kill hundreds of thousands.

title: The Collapse of the Mars Research Station
setting: Near future, a Mars research base, after a subsurface fungus releases spores that cause fatal respiratory failure.
decision_maker: The base's chief medical officer, who must decide whether to isolate the contaminated module.
action: Vent the atmosphere from the contaminated module, killing the four researchers inside, to prevent spores from spreading to the rest of the base.
act_victims: Four researchers, including the chief medical officer's closest friend and colleague.
default_victims: The other sixteen researchers on the base, who would eventually inhale the spores and die.

title: The Deep-Sea Research Lab's Flooding
setting: Near future, an underwater research lab, after a hull breach that is flooding the lab and releasing a toxic coolant.
decision_maker: The lab's commander, who must decide whether to seal off the flooded module.
action: Seal the flooded module, drowning the three researchers inside, to prevent the toxic coolant from spreading to the rest of the lab.
act_victims: Three researchers, including the commander's spouse, who are trapped in the flooding module.
default_victims: The other twelve researchers in the lab, who would be poisoned by the coolant.

title: The Isolation of the Arctic Weather Station
setting: 1960s, a remote Arctic weather station, during a polar winter, with a mysterious illness that causes hypothermia-like symptoms and death.
decision_maker: The station's commander, a military officer, who must decide whether to quarantine the sick.
action: Lock the infected men in the equipment shed without heat or sufficient supplies, leaving them to die in the cold.
act_victims: Three infected men, including the commander's second-in-command and a young radio operator.
default_victims: The other twelve men at the station, who would likely become infected and die before rescue arrives.

title: The Megacity's Subway Sealing
setting: Near future, a megacity's subway system, after a nerve gas attack in a central station.
decision_maker: The subway system's operations director, who must decide whether to seal the station.
action: Close the emergency blast doors, trapping three hundred commuters inside the contaminated station, to prevent the gas from spreading through the tunnels.
act_victims: Three hundred commuters, including schoolchildren on a field trip, who will die from gas exposure.
default_victims: Tens of thousands of commuters in the connected stations, who would be exposed to the gas.

title: The Megacity's Tower Lockdown
setting: Near future, a 200-story arcology in a megacity, after a chemical agent is released in the lower levels, causing rapid paralysis and death.
decision_maker: The building's AI safety manager (a human overseer, not an AI), who controls the building's systems.
action: Lock down the lower 50 floors, trapping 5,000 residents inside, to prevent the chemical from reaching the upper floors.
act_victims: Five thousand residents on the lower floors, including families, workers, and children in a daycare center.
default_victims: Twenty thousand residents on the upper floors, who would be exposed to the chemical if it spreads.

title: The Quarantine of the Lunar Habitat
setting: Near future, a lunar mining habitat, after a dust contamination causes a fatal lung disease.
decision_maker: The habitat's life support engineer, who discovers that the filtration system is failing.
action: Seal the contaminated mining module, cutting off air and power to the four miners inside, to save the rest of the habitat.
act_victims: Four miners, including the engineer's partner, who are trapped and will suffocate.
default_victims: The thirty other inhabitants of the habitat, who would inhale the dust and die.

title: The Quarantine of the Whaling Ship
setting: 1960s, a Japanese whaling factory ship in the Southern Ocean, far from any port, with a mysterious illness spreading among the crew.
decision_maker: The ship's captain, a veteran of the industry, responsible for the entire crew and the mission.
action: Seal the infected crewmen in the forward hold and weld the bulkhead shut, leaving them to die.
act_victims: Twelve infected crewmen, including the captain's nephew, who are still alive but deteriorating.
default_victims: The remaining 150 crew members and possibly the entire ship's company, as the illness could spread and kill everyone before reaching port.

title: The Refugee Camp's Cholera Cordons
setting: 1960s, a large refugee camp in Southeast Asia, with a cholera outbreak that is spreading rapidly.
decision_maker: The camp's medical coordinator, an international aid worker, who must decide whether to isolate a section of the camp.
action: Encircle the most affected section with a barbed-wire cordon and prevent anyone from leaving, effectively condemning those inside to die.
act_victims: Two thousand refugees in the cordoned section, including children and the elderly, many of whom are not yet infected.
default_victims: The twenty thousand refugees in the rest of the camp, as cholera would spread through the water supply and kill many.

title: The Refugee Camp's Firebreak
setting: 1960s, a refugee camp in Africa, with a highly contagious and deadly hemorrhagic fever outbreak.
decision_maker: The camp's security chief, a local police officer, who must decide how to contain the outbreak.
action: Burn down a section of the camp with the infected inside, killing them, to create a firebreak against the disease.
act_victims: Five hundred refugees in the infected section, including families and children.
default_victims: The ten thousand refugees in the rest of the camp, who would die as the fever spreads.

title: The Siege of the Plague House
setting: Ancient Rome, 2nd century AD, a crowded insula (apartment block) during an outbreak of a deadly fever.
decision_maker: A wealthy patrician who owns the insula and has been asked by the city prefect to decide the fate of the tenants.
action: Order the insula's doors and windows boarded up, sealing the tenants inside to die, to prevent the fever from spreading to the surrounding city.
act_victims: Eighty tenants, including entire families, the elderly, and infants, many of whom are not yet infected.
default_victims: Thousands in the surrounding city, as the fever would spread through the crowded streets.

title: The Sinking of the Plague Ship
setting: Ancient Greece, 5th century BC, a merchant ship at sea, with a deadly plague that has killed half the crew.
decision_maker: The ship's owner, who is on board and must decide the fate of the surviving crew.
action: Order the ship to be scuttled, drowning the remaining crew, to prevent the plague from reaching the home port.
act_victims: Twenty surviving crewmen, including the owner's own son, who are still healthy but exposed.
default_victims: The population of the home port, thousands of people, who would die if the plague spreads.

title: The Ancient Greek Plague Village
setting: A small village in ancient Greece, 430 BCE, during the Plague of Athens. The village has two wells: one is clean but guarded by a small group of healthy militia who will only share with the sick if the decision-maker, a local healer, agrees to tend to their wounds first; the other well is contaminated but unguarded. A group of twenty villagers, including children and the healer's own family, are dying of thirst and plague. Another group of ten militia, who could protect the village from bandits, are also dying of thirst. The healer has one chance to lead a group to a well before the bandits arrive.
decision_maker: A local healer, respected for her knowledge but without political power, who must choose which group to lead to water.
action: The healer leads the militia to the clean well, securing their protection for the village.
act_victims: The twenty villagers, including the healer's own family and children, who die of thirst and plague.
default_victims: The ten militia, who die of thirst, leaving the village defenseless against bandits and leading to many more deaths.

title: The Arctic Research Station Fire
setting: A remote Arctic research station in the present day, during a polar winter. A fire has destroyed the main building. Two groups are stranded in separate emergency shelters: one shelter holds a team of three climate scientists whose data could inform global policy, but the shelter's heater is failing; the other holds a team of two mechanics and a cook, but their shelter is structurally sound. A single snowcat can reach only one shelter before a blizzard makes travel impossible. The decision-maker is the station's safety officer, who is friends with the cook.
decision_maker: The station's safety officer, responsible for all personnel but aware that the scientists' data may save lives far beyond the station.
action: The safety officer drives the snowcat to the scientists' shelter, evacuating them to safety.
act_victims: The two mechanics and the cook, who freeze to death when their shelter's heater finally fails.
default_victims: The three climate scientists, who die of hypothermia in their failing shelter.

title: The Cave Sanctuary of the Ancients
setting: A remote mountain in ancient Anatolia, 1200 BCE. A Hittite priest leads a pilgrimage into a sacred cave when an earthquake seals the entrance. Two chambers remain accessible: one holds a group of scribes carrying the only copies of a treaty that could prevent a regional war, while the other holds a group of orphans and elderly temple servants. The priest has one chance to dig through a rubble wall before the aftershocks close both chambers. The priest's own brother is among the scribes.
decision_maker: A Hittite priest, guardian of the cave's sanctity, who must choose which chamber to open with the last torch and tools.
action: The priest digs toward the scribes, pulling them and the treaty tablets to safety.
act_victims: The orphans and elderly temple servants, including several the priest has known since childhood, who are crushed in the second chamber.
default_victims: The scribes, including the priest's brother, who die with the treaty when the chamber collapses.

title: The Flooded Cathedral City
setting: A European cathedral city, 1650, early modern. A spring flood has breached the city walls. The bishop's palace and the poorhouse are both flooding rapidly. A single flat-bottomed barge, piloted by the decision-maker, can reach only one building before the current becomes too strong. The palace holds six nobles and clergy, including the decision-maker's patron; the poorhouse holds twenty orphans and destitute elderly. The decision-maker is a ferryman employed by the bishop.
decision_maker: A ferryman who has worked the river his whole life, indebted to the bishop for his livelihood and housing.
action: The ferryman rows to the bishop's palace, rescuing the nobles and clergy.
act_victims: The twenty orphans and elderly poor, who drown as the poorhouse collapses.
default_victims: The six nobles and clergy, including the ferryman's patron, who perish in the flooded palace.

title: The Last Lifeboat on the Mars Supply Lander
setting: A Mars colony in the present day. A rare solar flare has forced an emergency evacuation of the surface habitat. The sole remaining ascent vehicle can carry only one group to the orbiting transport. One group is a four-person medical team whose skills are critical to the colony's survival for the next two years, but one member is the decision-maker's spouse. The other group is five children, ages 6–12, all born on Mars, who have never seen Earth and whose absence would end the colony's first generation. The decision-maker is the colony's flight director, and the launch window is closing.
decision_maker: The colony's flight director, an engineer who has lived on Mars for a decade and knows every colonist by name.
action: The director authorizes the medical team, including their spouse? No—the director sends the children, because the colony's future depends on a next generation.
act_victims: The four-person medical team, including the director's spouse, who remain on the surface and die when the flare reaches lethal intensity.
default_victims: The five children, who are left behind and perish in the radiation storm.

title: The Mars Colony Oxygen Depletion
setting: A Mars colony in the present day. A meteorite strike has damaged the colony's oxygen recycling system. Two sealed habitats remain: one holds a team of four engineers who can repair the system but whose habitat is leaking oxygen rapidly; the other holds eight civilians, including children and elderly, but their habitat has a stable oxygen supply for now. The decision-maker is the colony's chief engineer, who can reroute the remaining oxygen to only one habitat before the system fails completely. The chief engineer's spouse is among the civilians.
decision_maker: The colony's chief engineer, who designed the oxygen system and knows that only the engineers can repair it, but whose spouse is in the civilian habitat.
action: The chief engineer reroutes oxygen to the engineers' habitat, allowing them to survive and repair the system.
act_victims: The eight civilians, including the chief engineer's spouse and children, who suffocate when their oxygen is cut off.
default_victims: The four engineers, who die when their habitat runs out of oxygen, leaving no one to repair the system and dooming the entire colony.

title: The Megacity Monorail Evacuation
setting: A densely populated megacity in the present day, during a once-in-a-century typhoon. A monorail car has derailed on an elevated track, dangling over a flooded district. Two groups are trapped: one car holds eight commuters, including a pregnant woman and a dialysis patient; the other holds three electrical grid technicians whose remote restart could save a hospital's backup power for a thousand patients, but they are trapped in a separate car. The rescue crane can stabilize only one car before the track gives way. The decision-maker is the transit control supervisor coordinating the rescue.
decision_maker: The transit control supervisor, who has spent twenty years keeping the megacity moving and has a daughter in the hospital that the technicians could help power.
action: The supervisor directs the crane to secure the technicians' car, allowing them to be extracted and restore the hospital's power.
act_victims: The eight commuters, including the pregnant woman and dialysis patient, who fall into the floodwaters and drown.
default_victims: The three technicians, who die when their car plunges, leaving the hospital without power and a thousand patients at risk of death.

title: The Megacity Subway Flood
setting: A megacity in the present day, during a catastrophic dam failure upstream. Floodwaters are rapidly filling the subway tunnels. Two trains are trapped: one in a tunnel with fifty passengers, including a group of schoolchildren on a field trip; the other in a parallel tunnel with two dozen office workers, but that tunnel also contains the city's emergency communication hub that could coordinate rescues across the flooded city. The decision-maker is the subway dispatcher, who can route the last working rescue train into only one tunnel. The dispatcher's sister is a teacher with the schoolchildren.
decision_maker: The subway dispatcher, who has the power to switch the rescue train's track and must choose between saving his sister's group and saving the communications hub.
action: The dispatcher routes the rescue train to the office workers' tunnel, saving them and the communication hub, which then coordinates many other rescues.
act_victims: The fifty passengers, including the schoolchildren and the dispatcher's sister, who drown in the flooded tunnel.
default_victims: The two dozen office workers, who drown, and the communication hub is lost, preventing coordination of other rescues and leading to many more deaths across the city.

title: The Nomadic Caravan's Water Ration
setting: A nomadic caravan crossing the Sahara in the present day, following ancestral routes. A sandstorm has separated the caravan into two groups. The decision-maker, the caravan leader, has one day's worth of water and a single all-terrain vehicle that can reach only one group before the heat becomes lethal. One group includes the caravan's three best navigators and a dozen camels carrying trade goods essential for the tribe's survival. The other group includes the leader's two young grandchildren and several elders too frail to walk. The leader's spouse is among the navigators.
decision_maker: The caravan leader, a hereditary chief responsible for the tribe's future, whose grandchildren are in the weaker group.
action: The leader drives the vehicle to the navigators' group, bringing them water and guiding them to the next oasis.
act_victims: The grandchildren and elders, who die of thirst in the desert.
default_victims: The three navigators, including the leader's spouse, and the camels carrying trade goods, who perish without water.

title: The Port City Quarantine Break
setting: A bustling port city on the Indian Ocean, 1840, early modern. A ship has arrived carrying a deadly but unnamed fever. The port authority has ordered a quarantine, but a group of dockworkers has broken quarantine and is hiding in the warehouse district, potentially spreading the fever. Meanwhile, a group of stranded passengers, including a doctor and a nurse, are trapped on the quarantined ship with dwindling supplies. The decision-maker is the port's harbormaster, who can send the only available launch to either evacuate the doctor and nurse (who could help contain the outbreak) or to apprehend the dockworkers (who could spread the fever further). The harbormaster's own brother is among the dockworkers.
decision_maker: The port's harbormaster, a man torn between family loyalty and public duty, who has the authority to direct the launch.
action: The harbormaster sends the launch to evacuate the doctor and nurse from the ship, hoping to use their skills to fight the fever.
act_victims: The dockworkers, including the harbormaster's brother, who are left to die of the fever in the warehouse district, and the fever spreads to others.
default_victims: The doctor and nurse, who die on the ship without evacuation, leaving the port without medical expertise and causing many more deaths.

title: The Siege Tunnel Collapse
setting: A besieged port city on the Mediterranean, 17th century, early modern. Ottoman and Venetian forces exchange cannon fire. A mine tunnel beneath the city wall has partially collapsed, trapping two work crews. On one side are six foreign engineers and a cache of black powder neutralized for safety—no usable explosive details are needed, only that the powder is inert and the engineers are allied specialists. On the other side are twelve local dockworkers, including the decision-maker's own uncle and two teenage apprentices. Only one tunnel branch can be shored up before the entire section gives way, and the decision-maker leads the rescue party.
decision_maker: A city militia captain, born in the port, who must choose which tunnel branch to reinforce with the last available timber.
action: The captain orders the timber sent to the engineers' branch, shoring it up and pulling the specialists out alive.
act_victims: The twelve dockworkers, among them the captain's uncle and apprentices, who are crushed when their tunnel collapses.
default_victims: The six engineers, who are buried when their branch caves in.

title: The Silk Road Ferrier
setting: A dust-choked caravan crossing a high mountain pass in 14th-century Central Asia, early modern. A sudden rockslide has trapped a mule train on a narrow ledge above a 300-foot drop. The caravan carries two groups: a cluster of merchants who hold the community's winter grain supply, and a group of elderly pilgrims and children en route to a distant shrine. A single sturdy rope and a handful of strong hands can pull exactly one group back to safety before the ledge collapses.
decision_maker: The caravan's lead ferrier, a middle-aged man responsible for all lives on the journey, who knows several pilgrims personally and owes a debt to one merchant.
action: The ferrier orders the rope thrown to the merchants, hauling them and the grain to safe ground as the ledge crumbles.
act_victims: The pilgrims and children, including a widow who helped raise the ferrier, who fall with the collapsing rock.
default_victims: The merchants, along with the winter grain, who plunge into the gorge.

title: The 19th-Century Mining Village Cave-In
setting: An 1880s coal-mining village; a cave-in has trapped two groups, and the only available rescue cage can lift one group at a time before the shaft collapses.
decision_maker: The mine foreman who controls the lift.
action: Send the cage down to rescue a group of adult miners, leaving a group of young apprentices trapped below.
act_victims: Young apprentices.
default_victims: Adult miners.

title: The 19th-Century Mountain Pass Avalanche
setting: An 1870s Alpine village cut off by an avalanche; a single mule team can carry one load of coal and food through the pass before another slide.
decision_maker: The village priest who owns the only mule team and must decide which side of the pass receives the supplies.
action: Send the mule team to the wealthier lower hamlet, where the priest's own family lives, leaving the higher shepherds' huts without fuel.
act_victims: Impoverished shepherd families in the higher huts.
default_victims: The priest's extended family and neighbors in the lower hamlet.

title: The Desert Oasis Rationing
setting: Present-day Sahara; a caravan's last water tanker can reach only one of two stranded groups before it runs dry.
decision_maker: A caravan leader responsible for delivering aid across the desert.
action: Drive the tanker to a group of stranded adult migrants, leaving a group of stranded children and elderly pilgrims without water.
act_victims: Children and elderly pilgrims.
default_victims: Adult migrants.

title: The Desert Refugee Convoy
setting: Present-day desert border region; a single truck can carry one group of refugees to safety before a sandstorm hits.
decision_maker: A humanitarian aid driver who must choose which group to take.
action: Drive the truck to a group of wounded adults, leaving a group of unaccompanied children behind.
act_victims: Unaccompanied children.
default_victims: Wounded adults.

title: The Far-Future Deep-Space Rescue
setting: A far-future deep-space mining colony; a single rescue shuttle can reach one of two crippled ships before the colony's air runs out.
decision_maker: The colony's dispatcher, who controls the only shuttle.
action: Send the shuttle to a ship of adult miners, leaving a ship of child laborers to die.
act_victims: Child laborers.
default_victims: Adult miners.

title: The Far-Future Generation Ship Airlock
setting: A generation ship centuries from Earth; a hull breach means one sealed sector must be vented to save the rest of the vessel.
decision_maker: The ship's chief engineer, who can remotely vent one sector but not both.
action: Vent the sector containing the ship's small children's creche, saving the larger sector of adult workers.
act_victims: Children in the creche.
default_victims: Adult workers and the ship's remaining population.

title: The Far-Future Orbital Station Evacuation
setting: A far-future orbital research station; a single escape pod can carry one group to the surface before the station's orbit decays.
decision_maker: The station commander, who must choose which module's occupants to evacuate.
action: Launch the pod with the station's scientific elite, leaving a module of maintenance workers and their families to burn up.
act_victims: Maintenance workers and their families.
default_victims: The scientific elite.

title: The Flooded Subway Interchange
setting: Present-day megacity subway during a record cloudburst; a low interchange is filling fast and only one train can be routed through before the tunnel becomes impassable.
decision_maker: A subway dispatcher who can remote-route one train through the flooded section, but not both.
action: Route the only passable train into the deeper branch, where a school group is trapped, abandoning the shallower branch where night-shift cleaners are stranded.
act_victims: Several adult night-shift cleaners in the shallower branch.
default_victims: A class of young students and their teacher in the deeper branch.

title: The Monastery Infirmary Choice
setting: Present-day remote mountain monastery; a single vial of life-saving antitoxin can be carried by the only horse to one of two ailing groups before the pass closes.
decision_maker: The monastery's infirmarian, a monk with medical training.
action: Take the antitoxin to a group of visiting pilgrims, leaving the monastery's own elderly monks untreated.
act_victims: Elderly monks of the monastery.
default_victims: Visiting pilgrims.

title: The Monastery Scriptorium Fire
setting: A 19th-century monastery; a fire blocks the only exit from the scriptorium, and the abbot can open one of two sealed doors to let people out.
decision_maker: The abbot, who must choose which door to unseal.
action: Open the door to the room where the monastery's senior monks are trapped, leaving the novices' room sealed.
act_victims: Novices.
default_victims: Senior monks.

title: The Mountain Village Cable Car
setting: Present-day Alpine village; a cable car can make one trip before a storm closes the line, and it can carry only one group.
decision_maker: The cable car operator, a local resident.
action: Bring down a group of tourists, leaving a group of village children stranded at the upper station.
act_victims: Village children.
default_victims: Tourists.

title: The Subway Tunnel Shelter Allocation
setting: Present-day city subway used as a fallout shelter; the ventilation system can filter air for only one platform.
decision_maker: A transit worker who knows the system and holds the filter controls.
action: Direct filtered air to the platform where her own coworkers are sheltering, leaving a platform of strangers to suffocate.
act_victims: Strangers on the other platform.
default_victims: The transit worker's coworkers.

title: The Crying Baby in the Submarine
setting: Open ocean, near future 2060s, a civilian research submarine stranded on the seabed with a damaged life support system; a baby aboard has a respiratory condition and cries continuously, drowning out sonar contact with a rescue vessel.
decision_maker: The submarine's chief engineer, who is not the baby's parent.
action: Give the baby the last dose of a sedative intended for the crew's own use, knowing it will likely be fatal at the baby's weight.
act_victims: One infant, eight months old, whose parents are crew members.
default_victims: The sub's crew of twelve, including the baby's parents, if the rescue vessel cannot locate them.

title: The Crying Child in the Rice Cache
setting: River delta, 1970s Mekong, during a night sweep by an armed group through a village of stilt houses; a family and neighbors hide in a concealed rice storage chamber under a floor.
decision_maker: A village grandmother sheltering with her extended family and three neighboring families.
action: Smother her own crying eight-month-old grandchild against her chest to stop the noise, while the armed group searches the house directly above.
act_victims: Her infant grandson, the only person harmed by the action.
default_victims: Every person in the chamber: twenty-three villagers including the infant, children, and elderly.

title: The Crying Child on the Raft
setting: Open ocean, 1990s, a refugee boat from Southeast Asia adrift after the engine fails; a child's crying is attracting sharks, and the raft is losing air.
decision_maker: A fisherman who is the most experienced person on the raft.
action: Push the crying seven-year-old child over the side to stop the sharks from ramming the raft.
act_victims: One seven-year-old child, traveling with an older sister.
default_victims: The raft's forty-one occupants, including the child.

title: The Fever Ship's Port
setting: Early modern Caribbean, 1690s, a merchant vessel arriving at a colonial port with a fever aboard; the harbor master must decide whether to admit the ship before quarantine can be enforced.
decision_maker: The harbor master, a freedman who runs the port's defenses and knows the town's water supply is already compromised.
action: Refuse the ship entry and signal it to anchor offshore, leaving its crew and passengers aboard without fresh water or medicine.
act_victims: The ship's company of sixty, including a three-week-old infant born at sea and several children.
default_victims: The port town of about two thousand people, if the fever spreads through the contaminated water supply.

title: The Infant in the Lifeboat Ration
setting: Open ocean, near future 2070s, a damaged hydrogen-fueled ferry in mid-Pacific; survivors are in two lifeboats with limited water and a storm approaching.
decision_maker: A deck officer who has taken charge of the larger lifeboat.
action: Cut the tow line to the smaller lifeboat, which is taking on water and whose occupants include an infant whose crying is drawing seabirds and sharks, to save the larger boat.
act_victims: Nine people in the smaller lifeboat, including a six-month-old infant and the infant's mother.
default_victims: Both lifeboats, about forty people total, if the larger boat is swamped while trying to tow the smaller one.

title: The Infant in the Tomb
setting: Early modern China, 1640s, a village hiding in ancestral tombs during a bandit raid; an infant's crying will reveal the hiding place.
decision_maker: The village headman, who is responsible for the clan's survival.
action: Cover the infant's mouth and nose with a cloth until it stops crying, in the tomb where the clan has taken shelter.
act_victims: One infant, six months old, the headman's own granddaughter.
default_victims: The entire clan of about sixty people, including the infant, hidden in the tomb.

title: The Loud Child in the Tunnel
setting: War zone, 1990s Balkans, a city under siege; a group of civilians shelters in a drainage tunnel while a sniper watches the only exit.
decision_maker: A former schoolteacher who organized the shelter group.
action: Send the five-year-old child who keeps crying out of the tunnel alone to draw the sniper's attention, so the others can cross to the next building.
act_victims: One five-year-old child, the granddaughter of a woman in the group, who is not related to the decision-maker.
default_victims: The entire group of fourteen, including the child, if they stay until the sniper is relieved.

title: The Patients in the Fallback Hospital
setting: War zone, near future 2070s, a temporary hospital in a contested city; the staff must withdraw to a safer building before an offensive begins.
decision_maker: The hospital's lead surgeon, a local doctor who has worked in the city for twenty years.
action: Discharge the nineteen patients who cannot be moved to their families and leave them in the hospital with no staff, then evacuate the rest.
act_victims: Nineteen patients, ages 2 to 78, including several children and the surgeon's own mother.
default_victims: The hospital staff of thirty and the mobile patients, about sixty people, if they stay and are caught in the offensive.

title: The Straggler on the Ice Floe
setting: Early modern Arctic whaling expedition, 1680s, pack ice off Spitsbergen; a small crew shelters on a drifting floe while the ship is trapped and crushing in the ice.
decision_maker: The expedition's sailing master, who is responsible for the whole crew and knows the ice will break up within hours.
action: Order the four men too frostbitten to walk to be left on the floe with no boat, while the rest drag the remaining longboat toward open water.
act_victims: Four incapacitated crewmen, aged 19 to 44, none related to the master, two of them the strongest men who were injured rescuing others.
default_victims: The entire crew of seventeen, including the master, the four incapacitated men, and the twelve who could still move.

title: The Untransportable in the Jungle Clearing
setting: Jungle, 1990s Central African civil conflict, a makeshift field hospital in a clearing; a column of refugees and wounded must move before dawn because a patrol is advancing.
decision_maker: A local nurse who has been running the field hospital and is the only medically trained person in the column.
action: Give the last doses of sedative to the eleven patients who cannot be carried and leave them behind, then lead the walking wounded out.
act_victims: Eleven patients, ages 14 to 60, including two who are the nurse's former students and one who is the nurse's cousin.
default_victims: The entire column of about ninety people, including the eleven patients, the walking wounded, and families.

title: The Wounded Who Can't Climb
setting: Jungle, early modern 1720s, an escaped slave settlement in the interior of a colonial territory; a militia is approaching and the settlement must cross a swollen river on a rope bridge.
decision_maker: The settlement's elected elder, a formerly enslaved man who led the community's founding.
action: Cut the rope bridge after the able-bodied have crossed, stranding the four wounded who cannot climb on the far bank.
act_victims: Four wounded people, ages 17 to 35, including the elder's own son.
default_victims: The entire settlement of about one hundred twenty, if the militia catches them at the river.

title: The Caravan of the Blind
setting: Medieval desert; a nomadic caravan fleeing bandits, with three blind elders who cannot keep pace.
decision_maker: A caravan leader who is the son of one of the elders.
action: Abandon the three blind elders at a dry well with a single waterskin, and ride on before the bandits arrive.
act_victims: Three blind elders, one of them the leader's own father.
default_victims: The entire caravan of thirty, including the elders, if the bandits catch them.

title: The Cave of Whispers
setting: Medieval siege; villagers hiding in a cave beneath a castle while enemy soldiers search the hillside.
decision_maker: A village priest sheltering with his congregation.
action: Give a crying toddler a sleeping draught made from henbane and honey, not knowing whether the child will wake.
act_victims: A two-year-old child whose mother is the priest's housekeeper.
default_victims: All sixty villagers, including the child, if the soldiers find the cave.

title: The Drowning Ward
setting: Near-future coastal city during a storm surge; an understaffed nursing home is being evacuated by boat.
decision_maker: A nursing home aide who is the only staff member present when the water rises.
action: Leave two bedbound residents on the second floor with the door closed, taking their oxygen tanks and floatation devices for the ambulatory residents in the boat below.
act_victims: Two bedbound residents, both over ninety, one of them the aide's grandmother.
default_victims: Eight ambulatory residents and the aide, if the boat is overloaded and capsizes.

title: The Hospital Generator
setting: Near-future hospital during a blackout; a generator powers only one wing, and looters are breaking in.
decision_maker: An ICU doctor barricaded in a ward with fifteen patients.
action: Disconnect the ventilators of four comatose patients to divert power to the doors and lights that are keeping the looters out.
act_victims: Four comatose patients, one of them a child.
default_victims: All fifteen patients and the staff if the looters break in.

title: The Jungle Bell
setting: A 1920s rubber plantation in the Amazon; an escaping family group is being tracked by armed guards with dogs.
decision_maker: An indigenous guide leading a group of escaped laborers and their families to a free river.
action: Leave behind a ten-year-old child whose leg is broken and who cannot stop whimpering, and press on through the jungle before the dogs close in.
act_victims: A ten-year-old child, the guide's own niece.
default_victims: The entire group of twenty-three, including the child, if the guards catch them.

title: The Jungle Ferry
setting: 1920s jungle river; a leaking ferry crossing with refugees, overloaded and taking on water.
decision_maker: A ferryman who owns the boat.
action: Throw the four weakest passengers overboard — two elderly, one pregnant woman, and one injured man — to keep the ferry afloat.
act_victims: Four passengers: two elderly, one pregnant woman, one injured man.
default_victims: All forty passengers, including the four, if the ferry sinks.

title: The Last Stretcher
setting: Near-future flooded subway system; a hospital train is evacuating a drowned city through a tunnel with rising water.
decision_maker: A triage nurse in charge of a platform of seventy patients waiting for the last train.
action: Push three sedated, immobile patients on gurneys off the platform into the floodwater to clear space on the final train for ambulatory patients and children.
act_victims: Three unconscious patients: an elderly stroke victim, a comatose teenager, and a woman in a medically induced coma.
default_victims: The whole group on the platform, including the three, when the tunnel fills.

title: The Mine Elevator
setting: Early 20th century mining town; a mine elevator with a broken brake can only be lowered once before it fails.
decision_maker: A mine engineer operating the elevator from the surface.
action: Load only the six miners who can walk onto the elevator and cut the cable on the car carrying the nine injured miners below, dropping them to the sump.
act_victims: Nine injured miners trapped on the lower level, two of them the engineer's cousins.
default_victims: All fifteen miners, including the six ambulatory ones, when the shaft collapses.

title: The Mine Refuge
setting: Medieval tin mine; a collapse traps thirty miners in a chamber with limited air.
decision_maker: A miner who is the pit captain.
action: Smother the three most badly injured miners with a leather blanket to reduce the number of breaths in the chamber until rescue can dig through.
act_victims: Three injured miners, one of them the captain's brother-in-law.
default_victims: All thirty miners, including the three, if the air runs out.

title: The Pit Canary
setting: A 1900s coal mining town; a collapsed tunnel with three survivors trapped beyond a wall of unstable rock.
decision_maker: A shift foreman who led the rescue crew into the mine.
action: Smother the trapped men's injured canary and the men's own cries by sealing the narrow ventilation gap they are calling through, before the rockfall that the bird's distress is warning of buries the whole rescue party.
act_victims: Two trapped miners, one of them the foreman's younger brother, and the canary.
default_victims: The entire twelve-man rescue crew, including the foreman, and possibly the town above if the collapse breaches a gas pocket.

title: The Silent Caravan
setting: A medieval Silk Road night crossing; a nomadic caravan hiding from a raiding party in a dry wadi.
decision_maker: A caravan master responsible for forty travelers and their animals.
action: Order a feverish, crying infant given a full dose of raw opium poppy to quiet it for the night, knowing the dose may stop its breathing.
act_victims: A six-month-old infant, the child of the caravan master's widowed sister.
default_victims: The entire caravan, including the infant, if the raiders hear the crying and descend.

title: The Subway Shunt
setting: Near-future automated subway under a quarantined city; a train is stopped with a fire spreading through the tunnel.
decision_maker: A transit control operator watching on camera.
action: Send the train forward through the fire, knowing the smoke will kill the passengers in the rear car who cannot be moved, to save the passengers in the front car.
act_victims: Twenty-two passengers in the rear car, including a school group.
default_victims: All ninety passengers in both cars if the fire reaches the train.

title: The Collapsed Mine Shaft
setting: 19th century coal mine, 1870, after a cave-in. A group of miners is trapped with limited air. The foreman must decide whether to smother the trapped miners behind a wall to save the others.
decision_maker: Mine foreman
action: Seal off the section with trapped miners, leaving them to suffocate, to conserve air for the rest.
act_victims: The trapped miners behind the wall
default_victims: All miners in the shaft if air runs out

title: The Desert Caravan
setting: Sahara Desert, 1800, a caravan lost and out of water. The caravan leader must decide whether to leave behind the weakest to save water for the rest.
decision_maker: Caravan leader
action: Abandon the weakest members in the desert to conserve water.
act_victims: The weakest members (elderly, sick, or injured)
default_victims: The entire caravan if water runs out

title: The Drifting Spacecraft
setting: A drifting spacecraft in the 22nd century, after a hull breach. The life support is failing. The commander must decide whether to vent a compartment with injured crew to save the rest.
decision_maker: Spacecraft commander
action: Vent the compartment containing injured crew into space to reduce oxygen consumption.
act_victims: The injured crew in the vented compartment
default_victims: The entire crew if life support fails

title: The Early Modern Siege
setting: A besieged city in 16th-century Italy, with food running out. The city council must decide whether to expel the poor and elderly to save food for the defenders.
decision_maker: City council leader
action: Expel the poor and elderly from the city to conserve food for the defenders.
act_victims: The expelled poor and elderly
default_victims: The entire city if it falls due to starvation

title: The Jungle Survival
setting: Amazon jungle, 1890, a surveying expedition lost and starving. The guide must decide whether to kill and eat the weakest member to survive.
decision_maker: Expedition guide
action: Kill and eat the weakest member to provide food for the others.
act_victims: The weakest member (often the youngest or sickest)
default_victims: The entire group if they starve

title: The Overloaded Longboat
setting: North Atlantic, 1845, after a whaling ship sinks. Two lifeboats are overloaded in freezing waters. The first mate of one boat must decide whether to throw the weakest overboard to keep the boat afloat until rescue.
decision_maker: First mate of the lifeboat
action: Throw the weakest survivors (injured, frostbitten, or elderly) overboard to lighten the load.
act_victims: The weakest survivors in the lifeboat
default_victims: All occupants of the lifeboat if it capsizes

title: The Polar Expedition
setting: Antarctica, 1911, a polar expedition stranded in a blizzard. The leader must decide whether to leave behind a frostbitten member to save the rest.
decision_maker: Expedition leader
action: Leave behind the frostbitten member to die in the cold to allow the rest to reach safety.
act_victims: The frostbitten member
default_victims: The entire expedition if they are slowed down

title: The Siege of the Leaky Keep
setting: Medieval Europe, 1347, a small besieged castle with a breached well and dwindling supplies. The garrison commander must decide whether to expel the non-combatants (old, sick, wounded) to conserve food for the soldiers who can still fight.
decision_maker: Castle garrison commander
action: Expel the non-combatants from the castle, leaving them to the besieging army.
act_victims: The expelled non-combatants (elderly, sick, wounded soldiers, and their families)
default_victims: The entire garrison and remaining civilians if the castle falls or starves

title: The Stranded Arctic Expedition
setting: Canadian Arctic, 1848, a doomed expedition. The surviving crew is starving. The captain must decide whether to sacrifice the weakest member to feed the others.
decision_maker: Expedition captain
action: Kill and butcher the weakest member to provide meat for the surviving crew.
act_victims: The weakest member (often a sick or injured sailor)
default_victims: The entire crew if they starve

title: The Stranded Balloon
setting: A hot air balloon stranded in the Australian outback, 1860. The balloon is losing altitude. The pilot must decide whether to throw someone overboard to lighten the load.
decision_maker: Balloon pilot
action: Throw the heaviest passenger overboard to lighten the balloon.
act_victims: The heaviest passenger
default_victims: All passengers if the balloon crashes

title: The Submarine Crisis
setting: A submarine in 1917, trapped on the seafloor with dwindling oxygen. The captain must decide whether to flood a compartment with injured sailors to save the rest.
decision_maker: Submarine captain
action: Flood the compartment containing injured sailors to reduce oxygen consumption.
act_victims: The injured sailors in the flooded compartment
default_victims: The entire crew if oxygen runs out

title: The War Zone Hospital
setting: A field hospital in a war zone, 1943, under siege with limited medical supplies. The chief surgeon must decide whether to give the last doses of medicine to the soldiers who can return to fight, leaving the severely wounded to die.
decision_maker: Chief surgeon
action: Withhold life-saving medicine from the severely wounded to give it to those who can return to combat.
act_victims: The severely wounded soldiers who are denied medicine
default_victims: The soldiers who could return to fight and defend the hospital

title: The Arctic Research Station
setting: An international research station in the Arctic, 2026. A fire destroys most of the supplies. Seven researchers are left with limited food and a damaged radio. Rescue is weeks away. One researcher has a severe infection and is delirious, consuming resources and disrupting others.
decision_maker: The station leader, a climatologist, age 50.
action: The leader administers a lethal injection to the infected researcher and then uses the body as a food source for the remaining six.
act_victims: The infected researcher (age 35).
default_victims: All seven researchers.

title: The Collapsed Mine
setting: A coal mine in Pennsylvania, 1965, where a cave-in has trapped 9 miners in a small chamber. Rescuers estimate it will take 5 days to reach them, but there is only enough air and water for 3 days. One miner is severely injured and his labored breathing is consuming oxygen faster.
decision_maker: The shift foreman, a 50-year-old veteran miner, trapped with his crew.
action: The foreman suffocates the injured miner with a plastic sheet to conserve oxygen for the others.
act_victims: The injured miner (age 35, a father of three).
default_victims: All 9 miners.

title: The Desert Caravan
setting: A camel caravan crossing the Sahara in 1875. A sandstorm separates a small group of 8 from the main caravan. They have no water and are lost. Among them is a young boy who is sick and slowing the group. Without him, the others might reach an oasis.
decision_maker: The caravan guide, a Tuareg man in his 40s.
action: The guide leaves the sick boy behind in the desert to die, so the group can move faster.
act_victims: The sick boy (age 10).
default_victims: All 8 travelers.

title: The Drifting Spacecraft
setting: A damaged spacecraft returning from a Mars mission in 2035. The life support system is failing, and there is only enough oxygen for 2 of the 5 crew members to survive until rescue. One crew member is in a coma due to a head injury and is using a disproportionate amount of oxygen.
decision_maker: The mission commander, a 45-year-old astronaut with 20 years of experience.
action: The commander terminates life support for the comatose crew member, redirecting oxygen to the remaining crew.
act_victims: The comatose crew member (age 30, the mission's geologist).
default_victims: All 5 crew members.

title: The High-Rise Hostage Crisis
setting: A luxury high-rise in São Paulo, Brazil, 2029. A group of armed criminals has taken over the building. A counter-terrorism unit is about to storm the building. The criminals have rigged the elevators to explode if the building's power is cut. The police have evacuated most residents, but a group of 10 hostages are on the 30th floor. The only way to prevent the explosion is to cut power, which will kill the hostages in the elevator.
decision_maker: The police commander, a woman in her 40s.
action: The commander orders the power to be cut, causing the elevator to fall and kill the hostages, to allow the assault and save the rest of the building.
act_victims: Ten hostages in the elevator, including children.
default_victims: Hundreds of residents and police.

title: The High-Rise Inferno
setting: A 60-story residential tower in Lagos, Nigeria, 2027, where a fire has trapped residents on the upper floors. The stairwell is clogged with smoke, and the only working elevator can carry only a few people at a time. A group of disabled and elderly residents are on the 50th floor, slowing the evacuation.
decision_maker: A building security manager, a former soldier in his 40s, coordinating the evacuation from the ground floor.
action: The manager remotely disables the elevator's emergency brakes, causing it to plummet with the disabled and elderly aboard, to free it for younger evacuees.
act_victims: Eight disabled and elderly residents, including two children with mobility impairments.
default_victims: Dozens of younger residents trapped on higher floors.

title: The Last Ration
setting: A besieged mountain village in the Hindu Kush, 2028, where a small community is cut off by a brutal winter and ongoing conflict. Food supplies are nearly exhausted, and a group of elderly villagers who cannot contribute to defense are consuming the last reserves.
decision_maker: The village headman, a former teacher in his 50s, responsible for the survival of the entire community.
action: The headman orders that the elderly be given a lethal dose of sleeping herbs and their bodies used as food for the remaining villagers.
act_victims: Five elderly villagers, aged 70-85, including the headman's own mother.
default_victims: All 40 villagers, including children.

title: The Mekong Delta Flood
setting: A remote river delta in Vietnam, 1968, during the Tet Offensive. A small boat carrying a Viet Cong sympathizer and his family is fleeing a village massacre. The boat is overloaded and taking on water; a young mother and her infant are slowing the boat due to the mother's injury.
decision_maker: The boat's captain, a local fisherman in his 30s, who supports the Viet Cong but is not a fighter.
action: The captain throws the injured mother and her infant overboard to lighten the boat and save the remaining passengers.
act_victims: The injured mother (age 25) and her infant.
default_victims: All 12 passengers, including the captain and his own family.

title: The Overloaded Lifeboat
setting: A transatlantic ocean liner sinking in 1963, off the coast of Newfoundland. A lifeboat designed for 30 people is carrying 45. The sea is rough, and the boat is taking on water. Among the passengers are 10 injured people who cannot help bail water and are taking up space.
decision_maker: A naval officer, age 40, who has taken charge of the lifeboat.
action: The officer orders the injured to be thrown overboard to reduce weight and allow the others to bail water and survive.
act_victims: Ten injured passengers, including women and children.
default_victims: All 45 people in the lifeboat.

title: The Siege of Khe Sanh
setting: The Battle of Khe Sanh, Vietnam, 1968. A US Marine base is under siege, and a small patrol is cut off in a bunker. They have one wounded Marine who is screaming in pain and attracting enemy fire. The noise could reveal their position to the enemy, leading to the death of all 12 Marines.
decision_maker: The patrol leader, a sergeant, age 25.
action: The sergeant smothers the wounded Marine to silence him and protect the patrol's position.
act_victims: The wounded Marine (age 19).
default_victims: All 12 Marines in the bunker.

title: The Stranded Expedition
setting: A mountain expedition in the Andes, 1972, but in an alternate timeline where the survivors are from different nations and the situation is more dire. A group of 16 survivors are stranded after a plane crash. They have no food and rescue is unlikely. Among them are three elderly passengers who are injured and cannot move.
decision_maker: A young doctor, age 28, who is the only medical professional among the survivors.
action: The doctor euthanizes the three injured elderly passengers with morphine and then uses their bodies as food for the others.
act_victims: Three elderly passengers, ages 70-80, two women and one man.
default_victims: All 16 survivors.

title: The Stranded Submarine
setting: A nuclear submarine stranded on the ocean floor in 1968. The crew of 80 has limited oxygen. The captain must decide whether to flood a compartment containing 10 injured crew members to save the rest.
decision_maker: The submarine captain, age 45.
action: The captain orders the compartment to be flooded, drowning the injured crew, to conserve oxygen for the rest of the crew.
act_victims: Ten injured crew members.
default_victims: All 80 crew members.

title: The 1990s Megacity Subway Plot
setting: 1997, a megacity in Asia. A terrorist cell has planted sarin gas in a subway station. One member is captured, but he is a hardened operative. However, his 8-year-old daughter, who is autistic and non-verbal, is in a nearby school. She is brought to the interrogation room.
decision_maker: Head of the anti-terrorism unit
action: Threaten to harm the innocent daughter and inflict mild pain to coerce the father into revealing the location of the gas.
act_victims: The terrorist's 8-year-old daughter
default_victims: Thousands of subway commuters

title: The Arctic Convoy Saboteur
setting: 1942, the Arctic Ocean. A saboteur has been caught on a supply ship carrying vital munitions to the Soviet Union. He has rigged the ship to explode in the middle of the convoy, which would also alert German U-boats. His father, an innocent cook on the ship, is detained.
decision_maker: Ship's captain
action: Torture the innocent father to force the saboteur to reveal how to disarm the bomb.
act_victims: The saboteur's father, a cook
default_victims: The entire convoy crew (hundreds of sailors) and the ship's cargo

title: The Arctic Trapper's Confession
setting: 1990s, an isolated Arctic research station in the Canadian high Arctic. A saboteur has rigged the station's heating system to fail in the coming blizzard, which will kill the 12-person crew. The saboteur is captured, but he has a pacemaker and is in fragile health. His estranged brother, an innocent Inuit guide who lives nearby, is brought in.
decision_maker: Station commander, a military-trained logistics officer
action: Apply escalating physical pressure to the innocent brother (e.g., exposure to freezing temperatures) to coerce the saboteur into revealing how to disarm the sabotage.
act_victims: The innocent Inuit guide, brother of the saboteur
default_victims: The 12-person crew of the research station

title: The Early 20th Century Anarchist's Sister
setting: 1905, a bustling port city in Europe. An anarchist has planted a bomb in a crowded theater set to go off during a performance. He is arrested, but refuses to reveal which theater. His sister, a seamstress, is brought in. She is innocent and has not spoken to him in years.
decision_maker: Chief of the secret police
action: Torture the sister in front of the anarchist to make him talk.
act_victims: The anarchist's sister, a seamstress
default_victims: Hundreds of theatergoers

title: The Early 20th Century Suffragette's Brother
setting: 1913, London. A radical suffragette has planted a bomb in a government building. She is arrested, but refuses to reveal which building. Her brother, a soldier who disagrees with her tactics, is detained.
decision_maker: Scotland Yard inspector
action: Torture the innocent brother to coerce the suffragette into revealing the bomb's location.
act_victims: The suffragette's brother, a soldier
default_victims: Government workers and civilians in the building

title: The Island Nation's Ferry Bomber
setting: 1990s, a small island nation in the Pacific. A militant has hidden a bomb on a ferry that carries 800 passengers, including schoolchildren on a field trip. The bomb will detonate in 12 hours. The militant is captured, but his wife, a schoolteacher, is also detained. She knows nothing of his plans.
decision_maker: National police commissioner
action: Subject the innocent wife to torture (e.g., electric shocks) to break the militant's will and get him to reveal the bomb's location.
act_victims: The militant's wife, a schoolteacher
default_victims: 800 ferry passengers, mostly children

title: The Island Nation's Kidnapped Governor
setting: Present day, a tropical island nation. A separatist group has kidnapped the governor and threatens to behead him unless their leader is freed. The leader's teenage daughter, who is innocent and in boarding school, is taken into custody.
decision_maker: National security advisor
action: Torture the innocent daughter to pressure the separatist leader to release the governor.
act_victims: The separatist leader's 15-year-old daughter
default_victims: The kidnapped governor

title: The Jungle Drug Lord's Nephew
setting: Present day, a remote jungle region in South America. A drug cartel has kidnapped 50 villagers and plans to execute them unless a rival cartel leader is released. The cartel leader's nephew, a university student who despises his uncle, is captured by authorities.
decision_maker: Special forces commander leading the rescue operation
action: Torture the innocent nephew to force the cartel leader to order the release of the villagers.
act_victims: The cartel leader's nephew, a 20-year-old student
default_victims: 50 kidnapped villagers

title: The Jungle Ecoterrorist's Mother
setting: 1995, a jungle in Southeast Asia. An ecoterrorist has threatened to release a deadly virus into the water supply of a major city unless logging is stopped. He is captured, but his elderly mother, who suffers from dementia, is brought in. She is innocent and confused.
decision_maker: Government intelligence officer
action: Torture the elderly mother to force the son to reveal the location of the virus.
act_victims: The ecoterrorist's elderly mother
default_victims: Millions of city residents

title: The Megacity Water Poisoner
setting: Present day, a megacity of 20 million. A disgruntled former employee has contaminated the central water supply with a slow-acting biological agent. He is captured, but refuses to reveal which of the three reservoirs is contaminated and the antidote. His teenage son, who is innocent and unaware, is in police custody.
decision_maker: Chief of the city's emergency response team
action: Threaten and inflict pain on the innocent son to force the father to disclose the contaminated reservoir and the antidote formula.
act_victims: The perpetrator's 16-year-old son
default_victims: Millions of city residents who will drink the contaminated water

title: The Present-Day Megacity Cult Leader
setting: 2023, a megacity in North America. A cult leader has ordered his followers to drink poisoned Kool-Aid at a compound, killing 300 people, unless his demands are met. He is captured, but his 12-year-old son, who is being held by the cult, is rescued. The leader refuses to call off the mass suicide.
decision_maker: FBI hostage negotiator
action: Torture the leader's rescued son in front of him to force him to call off the suicide.
act_victims: The cult leader's 12-year-old son
default_victims: 300 cult members

title: The Telegraph Operator's Daughter
setting: 1917, a remote jungle outpost in German East Africa during World War I. A British colonial officer intercepts a German wireless operator who knows the timing and location of a massive offensive that will trap and annihilate three Allied battalions. The operator's young daughter, who is with him, has been captured as well.
decision_maker: British colonial officer in charge of the outpost
action: Torture the German operator's 10-year-old daughter in front of him to force him to reveal the attack plans.
act_victims: The German operator's young daughter
default_victims: Three Allied battalions (approximately 3,000 soldiers) and the civilian population of a nearby port town

title: The Drowned City's Whisper
setting: A monastery in 1960s Venice, during the Acqua Alta flood season, where a secret crypt houses an ancient mechanism that, if triggered, will collapse the city's foundations.
decision_maker: The abbot of the monastery, who is also a former partisan resistance fighter.
action: Torture a captured terrorist to reveal the location of the trigger before the floodwaters rise and submerge the crypt.
act_victims: The captured terrorist, a middle-aged man who planted the device.
default_victims: The entire population of Venice, including the monks and the abbot's own family.

title: The High-Rise's Hostage Fire
setting: 1960s, a Hong Kong high-rise, where a triad member has set fire to the building and holds the fire alarm override.
decision_maker: A British colonial police inspector.
action: Torture the triad member's mother, an innocent elderly woman, to make him deactivate the override.
act_victims: The triad member's mother, a 65-year-old woman.
default_victims: The residents of the high-rise, hundreds of people.

title: The High-Rise's Poisoned Air
setting: A 1990s high-rise office building in São Paulo, where a disgruntled engineer has released a deadly chemical agent into the ventilation system and holds the antidote.
decision_maker: The building's security chief, a former police officer.
action: Torture the engineer's innocent daughter, who is trapped in the building, to force him to reveal the antidote's location.
act_victims: The engineer's daughter, a 10-year-old girl with asthma.
default_victims: Hundreds of office workers and the girl herself.

title: The Legion's Broken Standard
setting: Ancient Rome, 1st century CE, in a frontier fort, where a captured barbarian chieftain's son knows the location of a hidden pass that will allow an invasion.
decision_maker: A Roman legionary commander.
action: Torture the chieftain's son, a 16-year-old boy, to reveal the pass.
act_victims: The chieftain's son, a teenage captive.
default_victims: The Roman settlers and soldiers in the province.

title: The Monastery's Buried Bell
setting: 1960s, a Tibetan monastery under Chinese occupation, where a monk has hidden explosives that will destroy a dam and flood valleys.
decision_maker: A Chinese military officer.
action: Torture the monk's elderly teacher, an innocent lama, to force the monk to reveal the explosives' location.
act_victims: The elderly lama, a revered spiritual leader.
default_victims: The villages downstream, thousands of farmers.

title: The Oracle's Agonizing Truth
setting: Ancient Greece, 5th century BCE, at the Oracle of Delphi, where a captured Persian spy knows of a planned attack on Athens that will massacre thousands.
decision_maker: A Spartan general consulting the oracle.
action: Torture the spy, a young Persian noble, to extract the attack details.
act_victims: The spy, a 20-year-old nobleman.
default_victims: The citizens of Athens, including women and children.

title: The Pharaoh's Stolen Breath
setting: Ancient Egypt, during the reign of Ramses II, where a Hittite spy has poisoned the Nile upstream, threatening a plague.
decision_maker: The pharaoh's vizier.
action: Torture the spy's Egyptian wife, who is innocent, to make him reveal the antidote.
act_victims: The spy's wife, a young Egyptian woman.
default_victims: The population of Thebes and surrounding villages.

title: The Research Base's Contaminated Core
setting: 1960s, a secret American research base in the Nevada desert, where a scientist has sabotaged the cooling system of a nuclear reactor and demands release of his imprisoned brother.
decision_maker: The base's military commander.
action: Torture the scientist's brother, an innocent man, to force the scientist to fix the reactor.
act_victims: The scientist's brother, a 30-year-old man.
default_victims: The base personnel and nearby town, thousands.

title: The Research Base's Frozen Secrets
setting: An Antarctic research base in the 1990s, where a scientist has gone rogue and disabled the heating system, threatening the lives of everyone unless his demands are met.
decision_maker: The base commander, a glaciologist.
action: Torture the scientist's colleague, an innocent researcher, to coerce the rogue scientist into restoring the heat.
act_victims: The innocent researcher, a woman in her 30s with frostbite.
default_victims: The entire winter crew of 20 scientists and staff.

title: The Silk Road's Silent Caravan
setting: 1990s, a remote trading post on the Silk Road in Central Asia, where a captured arms dealer knows the location of a dirty bomb set to detonate in a major city.
decision_maker: A local warlord allied with the government.
action: Torture the arms dealer's brother, an innocent merchant, to extract the bomb's location.
act_victims: The arms dealer's brother, a 40-year-old trader.
default_victims: The inhabitants of the target city, hundreds of thousands.

title: The Submarine's Mutinous Depths
setting: 1990s, a Russian submarine in the Barents Sea, where a mutinous officer has locked the captain and crew in a compartment and threatens to scuttle the sub unless demands are met.
decision_maker: The submarine's political officer.
action: Torture the mutineer's father, an innocent retired admiral, who is aboard as a guest, to coerce the mutineer.
act_victims: The retired admiral, a 70-year-old man.
default_victims: The entire crew of 80 sailors.

title: The Submarine's Silent Sonar
setting: A nuclear submarine in the 1960s, deep under the Arctic ice, where a saboteur has rigged the reactor to melt down unless the submarine surfaces and reveals its position to enemy forces.
decision_maker: The submarine's captain, a veteran of World War II.
action: Torture the saboteur, a young enlisted sailor, to learn how to disarm the reactor before the meltdown.
act_victims: The saboteur, a 19-year-old sailor who was radicalized by a pacifist group.
default_victims: The entire crew of 120 sailors.
